d: Install @rubenchodev/materix-react, import the base stylesheet, load Roboto and Material Icons, and wrap your app in MaterixProvider.

s.x: Materix UI for React ships as ES modules with TypeScript types. Styles come from the shared package @rubenchodev/materix-ui, which is installed automatically as a dependency.
Requirement Version React and React DOM 18 or later (peer dependencies) Node.js 18 or later Bundler Any bundler that understands CSS imports: Vite, Next.js, webpack, Rspack, Parcel…
pnpm add and yarn add work the same way. React is not bundled: your app provides it.

Import the base CSS once, at the entry point of your app. It contains the --mtx-* design tokens, the light and dark themes and the.mtx-root base styles. Each component imports its own CSS, so you only ship the styles you use.

Components use Roboto and the Material Icons font, like MUI. Load them in the <head> of your HTML: Self-hosting If you prefer not to depend on Google Fonts, install @fontsource/roboto and material-icons from npm and import their CSS next to base.css.

MaterixProvider combines the theme ( ThemeProvider), the language ( I18nProvider) and the.mtx-root container that applies the base typography. It is optional (every component works without it), but it is the recommended starting point. d: Use Materix UI in the Next.js App Router: global CSS in the root layout, 'use client' boundaries and getThemeScript to apply the theme before hydration.

s.x: Materix components render on the server and hydrate on the client. Interactive components and the providers use hooks, so they are client components ( 'use client'); you can still render them from server components.

Import the base stylesheet in app/layout.tsx (Next.js only allows global CSS there) and add the theme script to <head>. getThemeScript() returns a small inline script that sets data-mtx-theme on <html> before the first paint, so a stored dark theme does not flash light. suppressHydrationWarning is needed because the script changes <html> attributes before React hydrates. getThemeScript(storageKey?, options?) accepts the same storage key as ThemeProvider ( 'mtx-theme' by default) and { defaultMode, query }. Keep both in sync if you change them.

Pages can stay server components and render Materix components directly. Add 'use client' only to your own components that use state, effects or event handlers: Server and client render match Providers read browser APIs ( localStorage, matchMedia,?theme=) in effects after hydration, so the server HTML and the first client render are identical. The inline theme script is what avoids the flash meanwhile. You can also render it as a component: <ThemeScript />.

d: Light, dark and system themes with ThemeProvider and useTheme, theme without flashes, brand themes by overriding --mtx-* tokens, and the full token reference.

s.x: Every aspect of Materix’s look comes from --mtx-* CSS variables (design tokens) shipped in @rubenchodev/materix-ui/base.css. Components never use hard-coded colors: changing a token changes every component that consumes it. The React components use exactly the same CSS as the vanilla library, so a theme written for one works for the other.

The light theme is the default. The dark theme is enabled by the data-mtx-theme="dark" attribute on <html>; the CSS does the rest, without re-rendering React: The.mtx-root class (rendered by MaterixProvider) paints --mtx-color-background-default, --mtx-color-text-primary and the matching color-scheme (dark scrollbars and native controls).

ThemeProvider manages that attribute for you. It supports three modes: light, dark and system (follows prefers-color-scheme, also when the OS changes it). MaterixProvider includes it, so you rarely need to render it directly.

Prop Type Default Description defaultMode 'light' | 'dark' | 'system' 'light' Initial mode (uncontrolled). mode 'light' | 'dark' | 'system' — Controlled mode; pair it with onModeChange. onModeChange (mode, resolvedMode) => void — Called whenever the mode changes. storageKey string | null | false 'mtx-theme' localStorage key that persists the mode; false disables persistence. query string | false 'theme' URL parameter that forces a mode (?theme=dark); false disables it. target 'document' | 'none' 'document' document writes data-mtx-theme on <html>; none writes nothing (scoped themes). Initial precedence (uncontrolled):?theme= › stored value › defaultMode › light.

useTheme() returns { mode, resolvedMode, setMode, toggle, target }. resolvedMode is always light or dark (the effective theme when mode is system). setMode(mode, { persist: false }) applies a mode without storing it. Outside a provider it returns light and no-op actions.

With server rendering, the stored theme is only known in the browser. Add the inline script returned by getThemeScript() (or the <ThemeScript /> component) to <head> so data-mtx-theme is set before the first paint. See Usage with Next.js.

MaterixProvider with target="none" does not touch <html>: it writes data-mtx-theme on its own.mtx-root container, so only that subtree changes theme. Floating layers rendered through portals under <body> (menus, dialogs, snackbars) take the theme of <html>, not the container’s. For a complete theme with no surprises, keep the default target="document".

Override the tokens in your own stylesheet, loaded after base.css. Always declare both blocks, light and dark: Override every token in both blocks:root and [data-mtx-theme='dark'] have the same specificity. When <html> carries the dark theme, both selectors match and the last one declared wins. Since your:root loads after Materix’s CSS, a token you redefine only in:root will also override the library’s dark value. If you change a color in:root, give it its dark value in your [data-mtx-theme='dark'] block as well. Guidelines for choosing values: -contrast is the color of text on top of the main color: it must have a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 (WCAG AA). -dark is used for the hover state of contained buttons and FABs; -light for subtle backgrounds (the calendar range) and for the Snackbar action. -text ( --mtx-color-{color}-text) is the color for text and icons of that color on the background (text/outlined Button, Link, Typography…). By default it reaches 4.5:1 (WCAG AA): it is the main color when that is enough, or a darker (light theme) or lighter (dark theme) shade of it; data-mtx-contrast="mui" restores MUI’s exact values (see Color contrast). d: Language of the built-in texts (close buttons, pickers, pagination…): I18nProvider, useT, per-component locale, overridden strings and custom languages.

s.x: Components that render their own texts (aria-labels, the date picker, pagination, the Drawer close button…) take them from a dictionary. English ( en) and Spanish ( es) are included; you can override any string or register new languages.

Precedence, from highest to lowest: The locale prop of a component that supports it. The closest I18nProvider (or MaterixProvider) locale. The lang attribute of <html>. en. Regional codes are accepted ( es-MX, en-GB): texts come from the base language and dates and numbers are formatted with the full code through Intl. MaterixProvider accepts the same locale and messages props, so you rarely need I18nProvider on its own. Providers can be nested: an inner provider overrides the language for its subtree.
Pass messages, keyed by language, with only the strings you want to change. They are deep-merged over the built-in dictionary:
Register a dictionary once, at startup, outside React. Missing keys fall back to English. Components re-render automatically when the registry changes.

useT(component) returns a translation function bound to the current language. Use it in custom components that should follow the same language as Materix: t(key, params?, fallback?) interpolates {name} placeholders with params. Related hooks: useLocale() returns the resolved language ( es) and useIntlLocale() the full code for Intl ( es-MX).

d: Move from the vanilla library to React: data-* attributes become props, mtx:* events become callbacks, Materix.theme becomes useTheme and initialization disappears.

s.x: The React version keeps the CSS, the --mtx-* tokens and the look of Materix UI vanilla. What changes is how you describe and control components: React owns the DOM, so there are no data-mtx attributes, no auto-initialization and no instances to look up.

Both versions use the same data-mtx-theme attribute on <html>, so custom CSS written for vanilla themes keeps working. See Theming and Internationalization. Gradual migration Both packages share the same stylesheet, so a page can mix server-rendered vanilla markup and React islands during the migration. Load the CSS only once and let each part manage its own DOM.

d: A 12-column flexbox grid with five breakpoints (xs–xl), gap-based spacing in multiples of 8px (also per breakpoint) and alignment, for responsive layouts.

s.x: Grid splits the available width into 12 columns and lets each item declare how many it spans at each breakpoint, just like MUI’s Grid (v2: flexbox with gap, no negative margins). Use it to lay out pages, forms and dashboards that change their number of columns with the screen width. To stack elements in a single direction with a fixed gap you don’t need a grid: use Stack; to center and cap the page width, Container.

A <Grid container> with spacing and items with columns per breakpoint through size (MUI Grid v2 API). Resize the window: 1 column on mobile, 2 on tablet and 4 on desktop. A Grid with neither container nor a size behaves as a container (same as vanilla), and a Grid with a size is an item. Sizes can be written as size={{ xs: 12, md: 6 }}, as an array size={[12, 6]} (from xs) or with the individual xs, sm, md, lg, xl props (the data-xs … attributes of vanilla); the individual props win over size.
Each item takes n/12 of the width. When the sum exceeds 12, the next items wrap to a new line.
Mobile-first: each value applies from its minimum width upwards. xs 0px · sm 600px · md 900px · lg 1200px · xl 1536px. Always declare xs as the base.

spacing={n} separates rows and columns by n × 8px using CSS gap, like MUI Grid v2. There are no negative margins or item paddings, so the grid never overflows its parent and needs no overflow: hidden wrapper. Each column width subtracts its proportional share of the gap ( 100% · n/12 − gap · (12 − n)/12), so 12 columns always add up to 100%. Any integer from 0 to 12 is valid, plus the half steps 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 (4, 12 and 20px). Values outside the scale are ignored with a warning in development. Spacing only applies to containers.
rowSpacing and columnSpacing set the vertical and horizontal gap independently.
spacing, rowSpacing and columnSpacing accept an object per breakpoint (or an array from xs).
size="grow" (or true, e.g. xs as a boolean prop) makes the item grow and share the remaining space with the other growing items. size="auto" sizes the item to its content width ( flex: 0 0 auto).

justifyContent distributes the items horizontally ( flex-start, center, flex-end, space-between, space-around, space-evenly) and alignItems aligns them vertically ( flex-start, center, flex-end, stretch, baseline). The short aliases start, end, between, around and evenly are accepted too. direction changes the flow ( row, row-reverse, column, column-reverse) and wrap the line wrapping ( wrap by default, nowrap, wrap-reverse).
An item with container is also a container: inside it there are 12 columns again, with their own spacing.
A dashboard with metrics (1 → 2 → 4 columns) and a main block with a sidebar, plus a form that stacks on mobile. component renders the grid as any element ( ul, section, form …).

In vanilla, setSpacing(n, bp?), setRowSpacing(), setColumnSpacing(), setJustifyContent(), setAlignItems() and setDirection() replace classes and new items are registered with Materix.init(). In React the props are the API and new items are just new children.
With the classes written by hand the grid works without the component.

The grid is purely visual: it adds no roles and doesn’t change semantics. Use meaningful elements ( component="main", "section", "form") for the blocks you lay out. Reading and tab order follow the JSX, not the visual position. With direction="row-reverse" or column-reverse the visual order is reversed but the keyboard order isn’t: only use them when the order doesn’t matter. Check that the content remains readable at a width of 320px (WCAG 1.4.10): always set xs so the columns stack on mobile.

d: Materix global baseline: Roboto typography, theme background and text colors, box-sizing, visible focus and a light or dark color-scheme.

s.x: CssBaseline adds the mtx-root class to <body>, which enables the Materix style baseline: Roboto typography at 16px, the theme’s background and text colors, box-sizing: border-box across the whole tree, an accessible focus ring and a color-scheme consistent with the light or dark theme. It also imports @rubenchodev/materix-ui/base.css (tokens + baseline). Render it once at the top of your app; use ScopedCssBaseline instead when Materix lives alongside other styles. It isn’t a full reset: it doesn’t remove heading or list margins, nor does it normalize forms.

Render <CssBaseline /> once, next to your app. It adds mtx-root to <body> in an effect (SSR-safe) and removes it on unmount, unless the class was already there. Several instances are reference-counted: the class stays until the last one unmounts. Children, if any, are rendered as is. Equivalence <CssBaseline />, <body data-mtx="css-baseline"> and <body class="mtx-root"> are equivalent. Writing the class in your HTML template (or using MaterixProvider, which renders a.mtx-root container) avoids a visual jump before React hydrates.
On the left, a block with the browser defaults; on the right, the same content inside ScopedCssBaseline: Roboto 16px, 1.5 line height, theme colors and bold at 700.

Inside mtx-root everything uses box-sizing: border-box: a box with width: 100%, 16px of padding and a 4px border does not overflow its container.
Use Tab: buttons, links and focusable elements show the --mtx-focus-ring-color ring only when navigating with the keyboard. Text fields are excluded because their border already shows focus.

The theme is chosen with data-mtx-theme on <html> (or on any ancestor), usually through ThemeProvider / MaterixProvider (see Theming). The tokens change and.mtx-root adopts the matching background, text and color-scheme, so native controls ( <input type="date">, scrollbars) also look dark. Switch this page’s theme to see it.

ScopedCssBaseline renders a.mtx-root container (a div, or the element given in component) instead of touching <body>, for example when embedding a Materix widget in a page with other styles. Only that subtree receives the typography, colors and box-sizing. Scope A scoped container keeps its margin (only body.mtx-root gets margin: 0). The prefers-reduced-motion rule only reduces the animations of elements with mtx-* classes; the rest of the page keeps its own.
In vanilla, Materix.init(el, 'css-baseline') marks a container created at runtime. In React, render ScopedCssBaseline conditionally.
There’s no inner structure: the class is enough.

The focus ring only appears with the keyboard (:focus-visible) and has a 2px offset so it doesn’t cover the content. Text fields are excluded because they already indicate focus with their border. color-scheme makes native controls and scrollbars respect the contrast of the dark theme. With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the animations and transitions of Materix elements are reduced to 0.01ms. The baseline doesn’t change semantics: keep using real headings, lists and landmarks.

d: Centers page content with a per-breakpoint max width and responsive side gutters (16px on mobile, 24px from 600px).

s.x: Container is the most basic layout block: it centers its content horizontally, caps it at a max width and adds side padding (gutters) that grows with the screen, just like MUI’s Container. Use it to wrap <main>, landing page sections or a toolbar. To split columns inside it use Grid; to stack blocks, Stack.
A single <Container>. Without maxWidth the cap is lg (1200px), as in MUI. The shaded area is the container; the inner strip, its gutters.
maxWidth sets the cap: xs 444px, sm 600px, md 900px, lg 1200px, xl 1536px or false to take the full width.
fixed makes the max width jump to the minimum of each breakpoint (600, 900, 1200, 1536px) instead of growing fluidly. Useful when the design targets specific widths. Resize the window to see it.
By default the container adds 16px of side padding on mobile and 24px from 600px. disableGutters removes them, for example to make an image or a table touch the edges.
Container bounds the width and Grid splits the columns inside it. No wrapper with overflow is needed: Grid spaces items with gap.
An article page: a full-width header and a reading body capped at sm to keep a comfortable line length. component renders the right semantic element ( <main>, <article>, <section>).

In vanilla, setMaxWidth(), setGutters() and setFixed() swap classes on an existing element. In React the props are the API: change them from state and the component re-renders with the matching classes.
The classes work without the component (for example, in server-rendered markup).

Container is purely visual: it adds no roles. Use component to render the right semantic element ( <main>, <header>, <section>, <footer>) instead of adding an extra <div>. Gutters keep text away from the screen edges on mobile; don’t disable them on text blocks. Capping the reading width ( sm or md) improves legibility: 60–80 characters per line.

d: Stacks elements in one direction (column or row) with even spacing, alignment, wrapping, dividers and per-breakpoint changes.

s.x: Stack lays out its children one after another in a single direction and separates them with gap, like MUI’s Stack. Use it for forms, action bars, card lists or any block that stacks on mobile and becomes a row on desktop. When content needs columns that line up across rows, use Grid; to center and cap the page width, Container.
A single <Stack>. The default direction is column (like MUI) and spacing sets the gap in multiples of 8px.
direction: column (default), row, column-reverse or row-reverse ( col is accepted as a legacy alias of column). Reading and tab order still follow the JSX.
Scale 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 (× 8px) applied with gap: no margins on the children. Values outside the scale are ignored (with a warning in development).

direction and spacing accept an object per breakpoint ( sm 600px, md 900px, lg 1200px, xl 1536px) or an array starting at xs, like MUI. Each value applies from that width up. Here: a column with 8px on mobile, a row with 16px from 600px and 32px from 900px.

alignItems aligns on the cross axis ( start, center, end, stretch, baseline) and justifyContent distributes along the main axis ( start, center, end, between, around, evenly). CSS values are accepted too ( flex-start, space-between …).

divider inserts a decorative
between each pair of children: horizontal in a column and vertical in a row (also when the direction changes per breakpoint). You can also pass your own node, as in MUI: divider={·}. Dividers are recomputed automatically when children change (no refresh() needed).
With wrap the children move to the next line when they do not fit (useful for groups of chips or buttons). The gap also separates the lines.
A Stack inside each Grid item: the grid splits the columns and the stack arranges the content of each one.
A form action bar and a profile card built only with Stack. component="form" renders the stack as the form itself.

In vanilla, setDirection(), setSpacing(), setAlign(), setJustify(), setWrap(), setDivider() and refresh() mutate an existing element. In React you change the props from state; dividers follow the children on every render.
The classes work without the component; dividers must then be written by hand.

Stack adds no roles: use component to render the right semantic element ( <form>, <nav>, <ul> with <li> children…). Generated dividers are decorative ( aria-hidden="true"): the structure already conveys the grouping. If you pass your own divider node, mark it aria-hidden too when it is purely visual. With row-reverse / column-reverse the visual order flips but reading and tab order follow the JSX: use them only when the order doesn’t matter.

d: Action button with text, outlined and contained variants, three canonical heights (48/40/32px), palette colors, icons and loading state.

s.x: Button lets users take an action or confirm a decision with a single click: submit a form, open a dialog, send a message. Use it when the action has a text label that describes it. If the action can only be represented by an icon, use Icon Button; if it’s the primary, persistent action of the whole screen, use a Fab. To navigate to another page, pass href and the button renders an <a>. Button, Icon Button or Fab? Component When to use it Example Button Action with a text label; hierarchy through the variant. “Save”, “Cancel” Icon Button Compact action recognizable by its icon, in toolbars or rows. Search, close, more options Fab The primary action of the screen, floating above the content. Compose email, create event
The component imports its own CSS ( button.css and progress.css for the loading spinner). Import @rubenchodev/materix-ui/base.css once in your app.
A single <Button> with its variant. The component renders a native <button type="button">, adds the ripple and manages the disabled state; there’s no inner structure to write.

Visual hierarchy is expressed through the variant, just like in MUI: Contained ( variant="contained"): high emphasis, filled and elevated. Reserved for the primary action; ideally one per block. Outlined ( variant="outlined"): medium emphasis, for important secondary actions. Text ( variant="text", default): low emphasis, for actions in dialogs, cards or next to a contained button.

Three canonical heights with size. Medium (40px) is the default and matches the height of a small Text Field, so both line up in the same row. startIcon and endIcon accept the Material Icons ligature name ( startIcon="add") or any node (an <svg>, another icon font). The button wraps them in <span class="mtx-button__icon mtx-button__icon--start" aria-hidden="true"> (or --end), adds material-icons when you pass a name, and moves them 4px towards the edge (2px on small) as in MUI. The icons are decorative because the text already names the action; an <svg> renders at 24 × 24px with currentColor. With iconOnly the button becomes square and circular (48/40/32px depending on the size). It requires an aria-label. For icons without a background, Icon Button is preferable.

Primary is the default color. color accepts secondary, success, error, warning, info and inherit in all three variants. With inherit text and outlined take the container’s color: use it on dark or colored surfaces (AppBar, banners, calls to action).

surface="primary" (or secondary) adapts the button to a background of that color: contained is inverted (paper background with primary text, mtx-button--on-primary) and text/outlined take the container’s color.

Buttons meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) by default: text and outlined use --mtx-color-{color}-text and contained warning / info use dark text. To get MUI’s exact colors, add data-mtx-contrast="mui" to <html> or a container.

Hover, visible focus (when navigating with Tab) and press (ripple) are applied automatically. disabled uses the native attribute: it dims the button, removes it from the tab order and blocks the ripple.

With loading the button enters a loading state like MUI’s loading: it gets disabled ( disabled, or aria-disabled on links), receives aria-busy="true" and shows a decorative 16px CircularProgress in the text color. loadingPosition picks the position: center (default; the label becomes transparent and the width doesn’t change), start or end (they replace the start or end icon without changing the width; without an icon, the indicator is added on that side). loadingIndicator shows a text (or any node) instead of the spinner. When loading goes back to false, the previous state returns: a button with disabled stays disabled. The button keeps its accessible name; to announce progress, add your own aria-live region.
fullWidth makes the button take up 100% of its container.
disableElevation removes the shadow of the contained variant in all its states.
Text is displayed as written. Add uppercase to get the uppercase style characteristic of Material Design 2.

If the action navigates to another URL, pass href: the button renders an <a> and keeps link semantics (open in a new tab, copy the address) with the look of a button. Since <a> doesn’t support disabled, a disabled link gets aria-disabled="true", tabindex="-1" and its click is blocked. To use a router link, pass it in component ( <Button component={RouterLink} href="/plans">). Any other element ( component="span") receives role="button", tabindex="0" and activation with Enter / Space.
A form footer with a single primary contained action and a table action bar with small buttons.
With fullWidth the buttons fill the column of a grid.

In React the state lives in props: disabled, loading and the rest are controlled by your state. ref points to the root DOM element ( focus(), measurements). Button doesn’t emit its own events: use onClick and the other native handlers.

Use <Button> (a native <button>) for actions and href for navigation. Icon-only buttons ( iconOnly) need an aria-label. d: Groups related buttons into a single piece with joined borders, separators and inherited variant, size and color.

s.x: Button Group joins related Buttons into a single piece: shared borders, separators between them and the same variant, size and color. Use it for sets of actions of the same level (text alignment, period filters, export formats) and for the split button pattern.

A <ButtonGroup> with <Button> children: the group passes its variant (outlined by default) to the buttons through context, computes their position ( first / middle / last) and renders role="group". Give it a name with label or aria-label.
variant="outlined|contained|text", as in MUI. Outlined overlaps the borders; contained separates with the dark shade of the color and moves the elevation to the group; text separates with a 50% line.
size="small|medium|large" is inherited by every button (32, 40 and 48px).
Each child accepts the Button props ( startIcon, endIcon). For icon-only buttons, put a.material-icons span as the only child and an aria-label: the group compacts their padding.
color accepts the palette colors and inherit; a child with its own color (or variant, size) keeps it.
orientation="vertical" stacks the buttons. It keeps role="group", which doesn’t allow aria-orientation; with role="toolbar" the group adds aria-orientation="vertical".
fullWidth takes the full width and splits the space evenly.
disabled disables every button of the group and sets aria-disabled="true" on it; a single child can be disabled on its own. disableElevation removes the shadow of the contained group.

MUI pattern: the primary action plus an arrow button that opens a menu with the alternatives. Give the arrow an aria-label and aria-haspopup="menu"; the Menu adds aria-expanded and aria-controls, and should anchor to the group so it aligns with its full width. In this demo the arrow opens a Menu anchored to the group ( matchWidth); choosing an option makes it the primary action and focus returns to the arrow.
With fullWidth the group adapts to the grid column.
The group is declarative: change disabled or render more children and the positions are recomputed on every render (no refresh() needed).

d: Circular icon-only button for compact actions in toolbars, cards and table rows. Always with an aria-label.

s.x: Icon Button triggers an action represented solely by a recognizable icon: search, close, share, open a menu. It is the right choice in toolbars, card headers and per-row actions, where space is limited. If the icon is not unambiguous, use a Button with text; if it is the primary action of the screen, use a Fab. aria-label is required An Icon Button has no visible text: without aria-label (or aria-labelledby) screen readers would only announce “button”. Describe the action, not the icon: “Delete invoice”, not “trash can”.
Pass the Material Icons name in icon. The component renders <button type="button" class="mtx-icon-button">, the 24px glyph (with aria-hidden="true") and the centered ripple.

icon accepts a Material Icons name (string) or any node: an <svg> (rendered at 24 × 24px with currentColor) or a Material Symbols glyph. You can also write the icon as children, which takes priority over icon. With href the root becomes an <a> without underline.

Without color the icon uses the active action gray ( --mtx-color-action-active), as in MUI. color accepts any palette color, or inherit to take the color of the surrounding text (dark or colored surfaces such as an AppBar).

Hover shows a subtle background, keyboard focus a ring in the primary color, and a press a centered ripple. disabled sets the native attribute (on links, aria-disabled="true" and tabIndex={-1}, and the click is blocked).
edge="start|end" applies a negative 12px margin so the glyph is optically aligned with the content edge, like MUI’s edge prop. Use it on the first or last item of a bar.

Wrap the Icon Button in a Badge to show counters and include the number in the aria-label. The button does not clip its content (the ripple is clipped by an inner container), so the badge is never cut off.

An icon alone is not always self-explanatory. Wrap the Icon Button in a Tooltip to show its name on hover, keyboard focus or long press. If the button has no aria-label, the tooltip text becomes its accessible name; if it already has one, the tooltip is linked as a description ( aria-describedby). Recommended for icon-only buttons MUI recommends wrapping every icon-only button in a Tooltip. A disabled button does not receive pointer events: wrap it in a <span> inside the Tooltip.
An editor formatting bar (a group of small Icon Buttons with role="toolbar") and per-item actions where each aria-label also names the object.
Inside a grid the Icon Button keeps its fixed size: it never stretches.
The vanilla methods become props: disabled replaces disable() / enable(), and ref gives you the DOM element. Icon Button emits no events of its own: use onClick and any other native handler.

d: Floating action button for a screen's primary action: circular (56/48/40px) or extended with text (48px).

s.x: Fab (Floating Action Button) represents the primary or most common action on a screen —compose, create, add— and floats above the content with high elevation. Use at most one per screen. For secondary actions use a Button; for compact actions in toolbars or rows, an Icon Button.
icon generates a circular FAB; adding label turns it into an extended FAB with text. The circular FAB needs an aria-label.

Circular (default): icon only, 56px. Extended ( mtx-fab--extended): icon and text, 48px tall. It is enabled automatically with label, or with variant="extended" if you write the content yourself as children.

With size. Unlike Button, the FAB’s default size is large. Size size Circular Extended Aligns with Large large (default) 56px 48px Medium Text Field (56px) Medium medium 48px 40px Large Button, large Icon Button Small small 40px 34px Medium Button, small Text Field

Combine icon and label: icon only, icon and text, or text only. A string icon is decorative ( aria-hidden="true"); icon also accepts a node such as an <svg> (24px). The label text is the accessible name of the extended FAB.

Primary is the default. color accepts the palette colors and default, a neutral surface with a border, useful when the screen already has a lot of primary color. inherit takes background and color from the container.

Hover raises the elevation from 6 to 12, a press shows the ripple and keyboard focus a ring. disabled removes the elevation and color (on links it uses aria-disabled="true", tabIndex={-1} and blocks the click).

position="fixed-br" and "fixed-bl" pin the FAB 24px from the bottom-right or bottom-left corner of the window (z-index of the SpeedDial layer). "absolute-center" centers it over the top edge of its positioned container, as in a bottom bar.
Inside a grid the FAB keeps its size; use it as the primary action of each card or column.
The vanilla size / color setters and disable() / enable() become props driven by your state. ref gives you the DOM element. Fab emits no events of its own: use onClick.
The CSS also works with plain markup (static HTML or server templates), without the ripple:

d: A box for selecting one or more options from a list or confirming a condition; supports an indeterminate state.

s.x: Checkbox lets users select zero, one or several options from a set, or confirm a condition (“I accept the terms”). It renders a native <input type="checkbox"> inside a <label class="mtx-checkbox">, so it works in forms, with the keyboard and with screen readers without extra code. If the option applies a change immediately, use a Switch; if only one option can be chosen, use Radio. Checkbox, Switch or Radio? Component When to use it Checkbox Several independent options, or a confirmation applied when a form is submitted. Switch Turning a preference on/off with an immediate effect, without a “Save” button. Radio Choosing exactly one option from a small, visible group.

One element with label is enough: the component renders the wrapping <label>, the native input, the visual box and the text. Native props ( id, name, value, required, autoFocus, form) go to the <input>.
Two sizes, as in MUI: medium (18px box, default) and small (16px with 14px text) via size="small", for tables and dense forms.
Without label, only the box is rendered. In that case give it an accessible name with aria-label or aria-labelledby (both are forwarded to the input), for example in a table’s selection column.
Primary is the default. Use color ( secondary, success, error, warning, info) to change the checked color.
Hover to see the border change color, press to see the ripple, and use Tab and Space to focus and check. The native checkbox does not support readOnly: to lock a checkbox use disabled.

helperText wraps the checkbox in.mtx-form-control and adds a.mtx-form-helper-text below it, outside the <label>, linked with aria-describedby. error adds aria-invalid="true" to the input, colors the empty box border and turns the helper red; pass the error message as helperText. You can also compose the pieces yourself with FormControl and FormHelperText: the checkbox inherits error / disabled and links the helper automatically.

The indeterminate state shows that only some child options are checked. As in MUI, indeterminate is controlled by the parent: the component keeps the DOM property input.indeterminate and aria-checked="mixed" in sync with the prop on every render.

Group related checkboxes under a label so screen readers announce it when entering the group: a FormControl with role="group" and a FormLabel (or a <fieldset> with <legend>). Use the same name to submit them together.
A sign-in form with a “Remember me” checkbox and a terms confirmation that enables the submit button.
With the Grid component a long list of options is split into columns: one on mobile, two from 600px and three from 900px.

With checked + onChange the parent owns the state; the vanilla instance methods become state changes ( toggle() → setChecked(!checked), disable() → disabled, setError() → error + helperText) and focus() uses inputRef.

d: Helper and error text below a form control, plus FormControl and FormLabel to share error, disabled and required state with the controls inside.

s.x: FormHelperText is the caption below a control that explains what to enter or why the value is invalid. FormControl groups a label, a control and its helper text and shares error, disabled and required through a context, so every piece updates together; FormLabel is the group label. Checkbox, Switch and RadioGroup already render these pieces for you with helperText and error; use them directly to compose your own layouts or to build new controls with useFormControl(). When to compose it yourself For a single control, prefer the helperText / error props of Checkbox, Switch or Radio. Reach for FormControl when several controls share one label and one message, or when you write a custom control.

d: Radio button to choose exactly one option from a visible group; RadioGroup reads and sets the group's value.

s.x: Radio lets the user choose exactly one option from a small set where it helps to see all the alternatives at once (plan, shipping method, frequency). Each option is a native <input type="radio">, so arrow-key navigation and form submission work with no extra code. RadioGroup shares a name (generated if you omit it), owns the selected value and adds role="radiogroup", a label and helper/error text. Radio, Select, Checkbox or Switch? You need… Use A single option out of 2 to ~6, all visible Radio A single option out of many, or little space Select / Native Select Several independent options Checkbox To turn a single preference on or off Switch
Wrap the options in a RadioGroup with label and defaultValue. Each Radio only needs value and label.
Medium (20px circle, default) and small (16px) via size="small" on each Radio.
Options are stacked by default; row lays them out horizontally and wraps them when space runs out.
color on each Radio ( secondary, success, error, warning, info); primary is the default.

disabled on the group disables every option (and sets aria-disabled on the radiogroup); disabled on a Radio disables just that option. error on the group sets aria-invalid and colors the empty circles.
helperText adds a.mtx-form-helper-text below the group, linked with aria-describedby. Combine error with the message in helperText to validate on submit.
The group needs a name: label renders a FormLabel linked with aria-labelledby; you can also pass aria-label or your own aria-labelledby.
A shipping method chooser that reads the selected value on submit.
The radios can live in any nested layout (here Grid): they keep reading name and the selection from the closest RadioGroup.
With value + onChange the parent owns the selection: group.value = 'low' from vanilla becomes setValue('low'), disable() / setError() become props and focus() uses inputRef.

d: Star rating to review a product or display an average score, accessible through native radios and the keyboard.

s.x: Rating lets the user pick a score from 1 to N icons (stars by default) or displays an average in read-only mode. As in MUI, it is backed by hidden native radios with labels (“3 Stars”), so it works with the keyboard, screen readers and forms without extra code. For a long numeric scale use a Slider or a Native Select.
A single <Rating /> renders five stars. defaultValue sets the initial value and name the radios’ name (submitted with the form; generated when omitted). Clicking the current value clears it ( null).
precision={0.5} allows half stars: each star contains two radios and its left half picks the x.5 value. Other fractions of 1 such as 0.25 also work; values are rounded to the precision.

MUI sizes through size: small 18px, medium 24px (default) and large 30px. Icons and size The built-in icons ( star, star_border, star_outline, favorite, favorite_border, thumb_up, thumb_up_off_alt, circle, radio_button_unchecked) are drawn as SVG, which scales without losing sharpness. Any other name uses the Material Icons glyph at its native 24px in every size: its font-size is never forced (Materix iconography rule). A custom SVG passed as a node scales with --mtx-rating-icon-size.

icon (filled) and emptyIcon (empty) accept a Material Icons name or any React node (for example your own <svg>). If you only set icon, the empty state uses the same icon in gray. Customize the color with --mtx-rating-color.
Hovering previews the value (the active star grows 1.2×); with Tab and the arrow keys it changes with a visible focus ring. readOnly displays a fixed rating ( role="img") and disabled dims it.
highlightSelectedOnly highlights only the chosen icon (satisfaction scales) and max changes the number of icons.

onChangeActive(event, value) reports the value under the pointer or the focused radio ( null on leave) so you can show a descriptive label, like MUI’s hover feedback demo. getLabelText customizes each radio’s accessible label.
A product summary with the read-only average and a review form that submits the value like any other radio.
Several rating criteria spread across responsive Grid columns, each named through aria-labelledby.
With value + onChange the parent owns the value; the vanilla instance members become state changes ( rating.value = 5 → setValue(5), disable() → disabled).

d: Lets users pick a value or a range by dragging along a track, built on accessible native range inputs.

s.x: Slider lets the user select a value (or a range) from a continuous or stepped scale: volume, brightness, price filters, temperatures. As in MUI, every thumb is backed by a visually hidden native <input type="range">, so the keyboard, screen readers and form submission work without extra code. For an exact number the user must type, use a text field with type="number"; for a few discrete options, use Radio buttons.
One element is enough: the component renders the rail, the track, the thumb with its native input and the value label. Name it with aria-label (or aria-labelledby).
Two sizes, as in MUI: medium (4px rail, 20px thumb) and small (2px rail, 12px thumb without shadow) with size="small".
The slider fills the available width, so decorative icons go next to it inside a horizontal Stack (MUI’s “Volume” pattern).
color accepts the MUI palette: primary (default), secondary, error, warning, info and success.
Hovering the thumb shows an 8px halo, keyboard focus shows the same halo and dragging grows it to 14px (pressed). disabled renders the slider in grey and blocks interaction.

The value label is a Material Design 2 teardrop balloon. valueLabelDisplay is off (default), auto (on hover, focus and drag) or on (always visible). valueLabelFormat accepts a template with {value} (the localized number, also used as aria-valuetext) or a function (value, index) => ReactNode; getAriaValueText sets a different spoken text.

marks (boolean) adds a mark at every step; an array [{ value, label }] adds labelled marks (labels can be any node), and the vanilla string syntax "0:0 °C,20:20 °C" works too. With step={null} the value can only land on a mark.

Each mark label is centered on its mark, so the labels at min and max overflow the rail by half their width. In narrow containers add marksInset: the first label aligns to the start of the rail and the last one to the end (bottom/top in vertical, mirrored in RTL).

An array value ( defaultValue={[20, 60]}) or range creates two thumbs, each with its own native input named {name}-start and {name}-end and labelled “Minimum” / “Maximum” (prefixed with aria-label or the aria-labelledby text). When the thumbs cross they swap, as in MUI; disableSwap blocks them and minDistance enforces a minimum gap. Form submission A range slider submits two fields: price-start and price-end for name="price".
track is normal (default), inverted (highlights the part after the value) or false (no track, useful with marks).
orientation="vertical" grows from bottom to top (200px by default; change it with --mtx-slider-vertical-length). The native input gets aria-orientation="vertical".
Inside a dir="rtl" container the value grows from right to left, dragging follows the mirrored axis and the left arrow key increases it.
A controlled price filter that updates a summary while dragging and submits both native inputs.
Inside a Grid each slider fills its column: one on mobile, two from 600px and three from 900px.

d: Toggle that turns an option on or off instantly, like a settings preference; uses role=switch on a native checkbox.

s.x: Switch turns a single option on or off with immediate effect: Wi-Fi, dark mode, notifications. It renders a native <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> inside a <label class="mtx-switch">, so it is announced as “on / off”. If the change only applies when a form is submitted, or there are several options to confirm, use a Checkbox. Switch or Checkbox? Ask yourself whether the user expects to see the effect without pressing “Save”. If the answer is yes, it is a Switch (“Dark mode”). If the value is submitted with a form (“I accept the terms”, “Subscribe to the newsletter”), it is a Checkbox.
One element with label is enough: the component renders the <label>, the native input, the track with its thumb and the text.
Medium (34×20px track, default) and small (28×16px) via size="small".
Without label, only the switch is rendered: give it a name with aria-label or aria-labelledby (forwarded to the input).
Primary is the default; color accepts secondary, success, error, warning and info.

Hover, focus with Tab, toggle with Space and press to see the ripple on the thumb. disabled blocks the control; readOnly keeps it focusable and announced but the user cannot change it (for values managed by an administrator).

Group several switches under a FormControl with role="group" and a FormLabel (or a <fieldset> with <legend>).
A preferences panel where each switch applies its change immediately.
Inside a Grid the switches are distributed in responsive columns.
With checked + onChange the parent owns the state; toggle(), disable() and setError() from vanilla become state changes and focus() uses inputRef.

d: Text field with a floating label, MUI variants, icons, counters, input masks and validation.

s.x: TextField lets users enter and edit text in forms: name, email, password, amounts or long comments. It renders the same markup as the vanilla component after initialization: the floating <label>, the notched border ( NotchedOutline, a fieldset with legend), the icons, the helper text and the counter, around a native <input>, <textarea> or <select>. To choose from a closed set of options use Select or NativeSelect.

A single element with label is enough. Native props ( id, name, type, autoComplete, required, disabled, readOnly, maxLength, autoFocus …) go to the native control; className, style and other attributes go to the root <div>. Without label, the placeholder becomes the label (as in vanilla). multiline renders a <textarea>.

outlined (default, with border and notch), filled (background and bottom line) and standard (bottom line only). variant="no-label" draws a full border with no label or notch, for search boxes and filters. With select, the field wraps a native <select> (options as children) and adds a single chevron.

Large 48px ( size="large"), medium 56px (default) and small 40px ( size="small"). The alignment rows show the field next to components of the same height: TextField small + Button medium (40px), TextField large + Button/IconButton large (48px), TextField medium + FAB (56px).

startIcon and endIcon accept a Material Icons name ( "email"), an image URL (rendered as ) or a node (SVG, Material Symbols). With a start icon, the label is translated exactly 32px so its first letter lines up with the typed text. startAdornment and endAdornment take free content such as a $ prefix or a kg suffix; as in MUI, a free startAdornment keeps the label floated and aligned with the start of the field (the prefix sits where the text would start), in all three variants, because its width is not the 24px of an icon.

The equivalent of MUI’s InputAdornment + IconButton. passwordToggle (only with type="password") adds the show/hide button with aria-pressed, aria-controls and a translated name, and calls onPasswordVisibilityChange(visible); the state can be controlled with passwordVisible. startAction / endAction create an IconButton with the given icon and call onAdornmentClick({ position, button, input }); name them with startActionLabel / endActionLabel. A mouse click does not steal focus from the field, and the buttons are disabled together with it.
color changes the focus color (label, border and underline): primary (default), secondary, success, warning and info. Red is reserved for the error state.

Normal, helper text, error with a message ( error + helperText), error without its own message (the helper turns red), required (asterisk), disabled and read-only. Hover to see the hover state and use Tab to see focus.

staticLabel keeps the label on top and the placeholder visible, hiddenLabel hides the label and the notch (give an aria-label), and borderless removes the border. margin ( none, dense, normal) and fullWidth work like in MUI.

multiline renders a <textarea> with rows (3 by default). autoResize grows the field as you type, and maxRows caps the growth before showing a scrollbar. As in MUI, minRows or maxRows turn auto-resize on by themselves.

counter="characters" | "words" | "both" with maxChars (or the native maxLength) and maxWords. A limit alone is enough to show its counter. When the limit is exceeded the field switches to the error state ( aria-invalid="true"); the counter is announced with aria-live="polite" and its texts are translated.

mask accepts a pattern ( 0 digit, a lowercase letter, A uppercase letter, * alphanumeric; any other character is a literal), a preset ( phone, phone-intl, credit-card, date, date-short, time, time-ampm, time-seconds, cpf, cnpj, zip, postal-code) or currency, configurable with currencyOptions ( prefix, suffix, thousands, decimal, precision). The value is formatted as you type and the caret keeps its position. onChange receives the formatted value and { unmaskedValue, isMaskComplete }.

Combine native validation ( required, type, checkValidity() through inputRef) with error and helperText. Inside a FormControl, the field inherits error, disabled and required and links the FormControl helper texts with aria-describedby. In uncontrolled mode, a form reset restores the initial value.
A sign-up form with Grid: one column on mobile and two or three on desktop, combining icons, masks, a counter and Buttons.

With value + onChange the parent owns the value. With a mask, value can be the raw value ( "125000"): it is displayed formatted ( "$ 1,250.00"). The vanilla instance methods become state: value / unmaskedValue = … → setValue(), setError() / clearError() → error + helperText, disable() / enable() → disabled, and focus() uses inputRef. Fields created at runtime are just new elements in the state (the equivalent of Materix.init() / initAll()).

d: Select with a custom MUI-style menu: search, multiple selection, bulk actions, groups, limits and icons or images in the options.

s.x: Select lets users pick one or more values from a list through a custom MUI-styled menu with search, multiple selection with checkboxes, bulk actions, groups and options with an icon or image. A hidden native <select> mirrors the selection, so the value is submitted with the form and required is validated by the browser. If you only need the operating system’s dropdown, lighter and better on mobile, use NativeSelect; for free-text input, use TextField.

One element with label is enough: the component renders the container, the floating label, the combobox, the hidden native <select>, the chevron and, in outlined, the notched border. Options are written as <option> / <optgroup> children (with data-icon / data-image as in vanilla) or passed through the options prop. Without defaultValue the first enabled option is selected, like a native select.
variant: outlined (default, with notch), filled and standard.
Medium 56px (default) and small 40px with size="small": the same heights as TextField and NativeSelect, so a small Select lines up with a small TextField and a medium Button in the same row.

startIcon on the control (Material Icons name, image URL or React node) and icon / image on each option. The icon of the chosen option also appears in the control. secondary adds a second line to the option in the menu.

color accepts the whole MUI palette ( primary, secondary, error, warning, info, success): it changes the label, the border or underline on focus and the selected option in the menu. color="error" does not set the error state.

helperText, error, disabled and readOnly (shows the value but does not open the menu). required sets the native attribute and the asterisk. Inside a FormControl the select inherits error, disabled and required.

In single selection, placeholder is shown while there is no value (the hidden select stays empty, so required validates it). An option with an empty value counts as “no selection” when there is a placeholder. Long text is truncated with an ellipsis without widening the field.

search adds a search box that filters by text and value, ignoring case and accents (with a 150 ms debounce). header adds a header and noResultsText the no-match message ( {0} = search term). Try typing “zz”.

With multiple each option gets a checkbox and the menu stays open. actionsBox adds “Select all / Deselect all”, and selectedTextFormat controls the text in the control: values (default), count, count > N or static (always the placeholder). renderValue replaces the text, for example with Chips.
<optgroup> (or an item with options) is shown as a subheader; disabled options and groups cannot be chosen, and maxOptions locks the rest once the limit is reached.

The menu is mounted in a portal with the control’s width, repositions itself on scroll and resize, opens upwards when it does not fit below (and keeps that side while filtering) and limits its height to the available space. It closes when the control leaves the viewport and respects RTL.

A shipping form in mtx-grid combining Select, TextField and Button: each field takes the full width of its column (one column on mobile, three on desktop). name is submitted with the form (several entries with multiple) and the form’s reset restores the initial value.

With value + onChange and open + onOpen / onClose the parent owns the state; the vanilla instance methods become state changes ( value = …, open(), disable(), helperText = …) and focus() uses controlRef.

The portaled menu registers itself as an upper layer: the Dialog focus trap lets focus into its search box, Esc closes only the menu (a second press closes the dialog) and its z-index stays above the dialog.

d: Text field with filterable suggestions: single or multiple selection with chips, free values, groups and asynchronous loading.

s.x: Autocomplete is a text input enhanced with a list of suggestions: the user types, the list is filtered (ignoring case and accents) and they choose with the mouse or keyboard. It follows the WAI-ARIA 1.2 combobox with listbox pattern. Use it when the list is long and searching is faster than scrolling, when values come from a server or when free values are allowed. For short lists without search, use Select or NativeSelect; for free text with no suggestions, use TextField. Select, NativeSelect or Autocomplete? One element with label and options is enough: the component renders the TextField (label, notched border), the clear and open buttons, the listbox in a portal and the hidden input that submits the option’s value under name. Type to filter, ignoring case and accents. Options can be strings or objects { value, label, group?, disabled?, icon?, description? }, the same format as vanilla. Any other shape works with getOptionLabel (and getOptionValue for the submitted key).
The same as TextField with variant: outlined (default), filled and standard.

Medium 56px (default) and small 40px with size="small", the same heights as TextField, Select and a medium Button. In multiple mode the chips become 24px and the field grows when they wrap onto several lines.

startIcon adds a start icon (Material Icons name, image URL or node; the label lines up with the text). On each option, icon shows a Material icon and description a secondary line. The trailing arrow is the popup indicator and the ✕ (visible on hover or focus) is the clear button.
color changes the field’s focus color (as in TextField) and the background of selected options: primary (default), secondary, success, warning, info (and error for the options).

helperText, error, disabled, readOnly (shows the value; it neither opens nor deletes), required (native validation while there is no value), loading (CircularProgress in the field and “Loading…” in the list) and the “No options” message (customizable with noOptionsText).

group on each option (or groupBy) shows a sticky subheader; consecutive options with the same group are grouped, as in MUI. Disabled options ( disabled or getOptionDisabled) are skipped with the keyboard and cannot be clicked. The time zone field uses its own objects with getOptionLabel, getOptionValue and groupBy.

multiple shows each value as a deletable Chip (its ✕, Backspace with empty text, or Delete / Backspace on a focused chip; ← / → move between chips). limitTags limits the chips visible without focus ("+N"), disableCloseOnSelect keeps the list open and filterSelectedOptions hides the options already chosen.

freeSolo accepts values that are not in the list: Enter confirms the text (in single selection also when leaving the field) and an option with the same label is reused. With no matching options neither the popup nor the open button is shown ( forcePopupIcon brings the button back).

↓ / ↑ open and move, Page Up / Page Down jump 5, Home / End go to the ends, Enter selects and Esc closes (and, closed, clears with clearOnEscape). Options: autoHighlight (highlights the first one), autoSelect ( Tab or blur accept the highlighted one), clearOnEscape, openOnFocus, disableClearable, matchFrom="start" and includeInputInList (the arrows go back to the field at the ends).

Listen to onInputChange (with debounce={300} the input reason waits until the user stops typing), turn on loading, fetch the data and pass the new options. filterOptions={false} leaves filtering to the server (and disables the highlighting). The demo simulates 800 ms of latency and aborts the pending request on every new search and on unmount. The selected value keeps its label when new options arrive: a defaultValue="co" shows “co” until an option with that value is loaded and then “Colombia”.

name goes to hidden inputs: one with the value in single selection; one per value in multiple selection (like <select multiple>) or a single field with valueFormat="csv" (and separator). required uses native validation (a typed text that is not an option is invalid unless freeSolo); the form’s reset restores the initial value.
It takes 100% of its column in Grid.

With value + onChange, inputValue + onInputChange and open + onOpen / onClose the parent owns the state; the vanilla instance methods become state changes ( value = 'matrix', open(), clear(), setOptions(), disable()) and focus() uses inputRef. value accepts an option, an option key ( 'matrix') or, in freeSolo, a string; onChange returns the option.

d: Date, time, date-time and range pickers with a calendar, MD2 radial clock, popover, modal or static mode, limits and formats.

s.x: DateTimePicker is a single component that covers DatePicker, TimePicker, DateTimePicker and their range versions (the aliases fix the mode for you). It renders a TextField with a mask and an end icon button, and opens a calendar or a clock. It follows the WAI-ARIA Date Picker Dialog pattern: an accessible dialog, a keyboard-navigable day grid and a radial clock operable with the arrow keys. Use it when the date or time must be valid and easy to pick; for a date the user knows by heart (e.g. date of birth) a TextField with mask="date" may be enough.

Pick the component for the mode. Every TextField prop ( label, variant, size, helperText, startIcon, name …) works the same way. The field also accepts typing: a mask matching the format is applied, and only digits, separators ( / -.),: and the AM/PM letters are allowed, depending on the mode. variant: outlined (default), filled and standard, inherited from TextField.
Medium 56px (default) and small 40px with size="small". The small field aligns 1:1 with a medium Button.

The end icon is an accessible IconButton ( aria-label="Choose date" plus the current value, aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-expanded, aria-controls) that opens and closes the picker. It depends on the mode; change it with endIcon and add another one with startIcon.
helperText, error, required, disabled and readOnly, just like in TextField. With disabled or readOnly the calendar button is disabled and the picker can’t be opened.
Focus the calendar button and press Enter, or type in the field and press Alt + ↓: focus moves to the selected day (or today). The full key map is in Accessibility.

Range modes pick the start and end with two clicks on the same calendar (highlighting the span on hover; a click before the start swaps them). In DateTimeRangePicker, after choosing the dates, the Start and End time tabs appear (09:00 and 18:00 by default); releasing the clock on the start minutes moves on to the end time. rangeSeparator changes the separator ( " - " by default). The value is { start, end }.

The time view opens in keyboard mode by default (editable hour and minute cards, with ↑ / ↓; Enter on the minutes applies and closes). With timeView="dial" it opens the MD2 radial clock; the bottom-left button toggles between the two. ampm (or a format with hh / A) enables the 12-hour format with an AM/PM selector. views ( ['hours', 'minutes', 'seconds']), minutesStep, minTime and maxTime are passed to the clock.

Popover (default): drops down below the field (inside the TextField, as in vanilla), anchors to the right or opens upward if there’s not enough room. On screens 600px wide or less it’s shown centered over a dark backdrop, with aria-modal and a focus trap. Modal ( display="modal"): a centered dialog with an MD2 colored header on any screen size. Picking a day does not close it; use OK. Static ( displayStatic or the Static* aliases): a calendar or clock embedded in the page, with no field and no OK/Cancel buttons; each choice calls onChange.

minDate and maxDate disable the days outside the interval; they accept a Date, YYYY-MM-DD, the field’s own format or today / hoy. shouldDisableDate(date) disables specific days (they are skipped while navigating with the keyboard). defaultValue (uncontrolled) or value (controlled) accept a Date, a timestamp, ISO text or text in the active format. Without format, the date order comes from the locale ( en / en-US: MM/DD/YYYY; es, es-MX, en-GB …: DD/MM/YYYY, resolved with Intl). format defines how the value is displayed and typed (and derives the field mask). Tokens: YYYY / AAAA year, YY short year, MM month, DD day, HH hour 0-23, hh hour 1-12, mm minutes, ss seconds, A AM/PM and a am/pm. mask replaces the automatic mask.

The texts (Today, Cancel, OK, accessible names…) come from the Materix i18n system: the locale prop, then the I18nProvider and <html lang>. Regional codes are reduced to their base language for the texts ( es-MX → es) while the full code is used with Intl (date order and accessible day names). Months and weekdays come from the dictionary when the language is registered and from Intl.DateTimeFormat otherwise (e.g. fr-FR). todayText, cancelText, okText and clearText replace the button texts, and actions chooses the buttons ( today, clear, cancel, accept).
A room booking form in Grid combining a date range, a time, a Select and a Button. name goes to the <input>, so the formatted text is submitted with the form.
value / onChange make it controlled; open / onOpen / onClose control the popover. The action ref is the equivalent of vanilla’s methods.

d: Toggle buttons group related options with exclusive or multiple selection; on their own they work as an on/off switch for a single action.

s.x: Toggle Button groups related options in a block with joined borders: text alignment, formatting, list or grid view. A ToggleButtonGroup handles exclusive selection (like a radio) or multiple selection (like checkboxes), and a standalone ToggleButton switches a single action on and off, such as marking a favorite. To choose among many options use a Select; for a setting that applies immediately, a Switch. aria-label is required on icon-only buttons A button without visible text needs an aria-label (or aria-labelledby) that describes the option: “Align left”, not “arrow”. Also name the group with aria-label or label.

A <ToggleButtonGroup> with <ToggleButton> children. Each button only needs value and, when icon-only, icon and aria-label; the group joins their borders, manages aria-pressed and passes its size, color and disabled state through context.
With exclusive only one button can be active and the value is a string (or null). Without it the selection is multiple (MUI’s default) and the value is a string[] in DOM order.

size on the group (or on each button). The icon keeps its native 24px grid; the padding changes (7, 11 and 15px, as in MUI). Each row aligns with the Text Field and Button of the same height. Text only, icon and text ( icon is rendered before the text) or icon only with aria-label. icon accepts a Material Icons name or any node (an SVG, for example).
color colors the selected state: standard (default, primary text) or a palette color.

Hover shows a subtle background, keyboard focus a primary ring and a press the ripple ( disableRipple turns it off). disabled on a button dims it; disabled on the group disables them all and sets aria-disabled="true" on it.
orientation="vertical" stacks the buttons; the up/down arrows then move focus.
fullWidth distributes the available width among the buttons.
enforceValueSet prevents deselecting the last active button, so the group always has a value (MUI’s enforce value set pattern), in exclusive and multiple mode.
A ToggleButton outside a group toggles its own state ( defaultSelected) or is controlled with selected + onChange(event, selected, value).
An editor toolbar: multiple formatting and required exclusive alignment, both controlled.
With fullWidth the group adapts to the grid column.
The group is controlled with value + onChange(event, value): writing value from code fires no onChange, as the vanilla setter.

d: Represents a person or entity with an image, initials or an icon; AvatarGroup stacks several and summarizes the overflow.

s.x: Avatar shows the identity of a person or entity in a compact space: a photo, their initials or an icon. Use it in user lists, card headers, comments or app bars. If you need a removable or clickable text label, use Chip; for a numeric indicator on top of an icon, use Badge.
Initials go as children, src renders the image and icon inserts a Material icon (a string is the icon name; any node, such as an SVG, is also accepted).
variant sets the shape: circular (default), rounded (4px radius) or square.
Canonical sizes of 24, 40 (default) and 56px with size="small|medium|large". A number sets a custom size in pixels (width, height and a font size of 45%).
Content is resolved in order: src (with srcSet, sizes and imgProps for the ), icon and, if there is neither, the children. Icons keep their native 24px grid.

Without color, grey 600 with white text is used ( --mtx-avatar-default-bg / --mtx-avatar-default-color, 4.6:1 AA contrast; MUI uses grey 400 at 1.8:1). color applies any palette color with its contrast text.

Avatar is not interactive: its states are about content. Without an image or icon it is in fallback mode (.mtx-avatar--fallback) and shows the children. If the image fails to load, the gets hidden, the root switches to fallback mode and, when there are no children, a.mtx-avatar__fallback with the initial of alt is added ( ● without alt), exactly like vanilla. A new src retries the load.

AvatarGroup overlaps its avatars. max (5 by default, minimum 2) also counts the +N indicator; total counts users that are not rendered; spacing sets the overlap ( medium = 8px, small = 16px, or pixels). Overflowing avatars stay mounted with hidden. The +N indicator has a translated aria-label ( {count} more) that surplusLabel replaces.
Online status with Badge and comment authors in a list.
Team directory in Grid: 1 column on mobile, 2 at sm and 3 at md.
The group recalculates on every render, so changing max, total or the children replaces the vanilla max / total setters and refresh().

Wrap the content with <Badge> and pass the value in badgeContent. The component renders the.mtx-badge__badge node after the children and positions it.
standard (default) shows the content, a number or a short text. dot shows an 8px dot and ignores badgeContent.

The badge wraps any element. With an icon button it can go inside, wrapping the icon (MUI pattern), or outside, wrapping the button. The badge is decorative ( aria-hidden="true"), so the number must be part of the button aria-label.
Without color (or with default) the badge is a neutral gray that adapts to the theme, as in MUI. The other values use the palette with its contrast text.

The badge is hidden (.mtx-badge--invisible, scale animation) when badgeContent is 0, null or missing. showZero shows the zero, invisible always hides it and max (99 by default) turns larger numbers into max+. max only applies to numbers or numeric strings.

An action bar with counters and an avatar with an online status.
Dashboard shortcuts in Grid: 2 columns on mobile and 4 from md.

d: A compact element that represents a tag, a filter, an input or an action; it can have an icon, an avatar and a delete button.

s.x: Chip represents a compact piece of information: a tag, an active filter, a recipient or a short action. Use it for tag lists, selectable filters or inputs the user can remove. For a primary action use a Button; for a counter on an icon use a Badge.
A single <Chip label="…" /> is enough. icon adds a start icon (a Material Icons name or any node) and onDelete adds the delete icon.
filled (default) uses a solid background; outlined uses a border and a transparent background.
medium (32px, default) lines up with the small Button; small (24px) suits tables and dense lists.
icon adds a start icon, avatar shows an avatar (it receives the mtx-chip__avatar class) and onDelete adds the trailing delete icon, which you can replace with deleteIcon.
color accepts the whole palette; on outlined the color applies to the text and the border.

A chip with onClick (or clickable) is interactive: pointer cursor, hover state, focus ring, role="button" and activation with Enter or Space. With component="button" the chip is a native <button> without browser border or padding. disabled lowers the opacity, removes focus and blocks the callbacks.
onDelete shows the delete icon and is called when it is clicked or when Delete/Backspace is pressed while the chip has focus. The chip doesn’t remove itself: you update your state.
Clickable chips that toggle between outlined (inactive) and primary (active), with aria-pressed as the accessible state.
Project cards in a Grid with their tags: 1 column on mobile, 2 at sm and 3 at md.
The label, the disabled state and the rest of the props are React state; ref points to the root element (for example, to focus it). The log shows the onClick and onDelete callbacks.

d: A thin line that separates and groups content in lists, menus and layouts, horizontally or vertically and optionally with text.

Alternatively, divider on each ListItem draws a bottom border.
An “or” separator between a social sign-in and the sign-in form (TextField + Button).
Metrics in a grid with a divider between the figure and its description.

d: Continuous vertical list of text, icons or avatars, with static or interactive items, subheaders, density and selection.

s.x: List groups related items in a continuous column: navigation menus, inboxes, settings or results. Each row can carry an icon or avatar, primary and secondary text, and a trailing action. For data with several comparable columns use Table; for a floating menu use Menu.
A List (a <ul>) with ListItem rows ( <li>). The icon prop adds the icon and secondary the secondary text; text children become the primary text (the equivalent of the vanilla single-element syntax).

Text only, with an icon, with an avatar and with primary and secondary text. avatar accepts an image URL (painted as an Avatar with avatarAlt, decorative by default) or any node, for example an <Avatar>; it is wrapped in ListItemAvatar (56px). alignItems="flex-start" aligns the avatar with the first line of long texts.

ListItemButton renders a <button type="button"> (or an <a> with href) with hover, focus, ripple and selection: clicking a row selects it and unselects the previous one within the same List. The selection is uncontrolled by default ( defaultValue, the value of the initial row) or controlled with value + onSelect. With selectable={false} the rows only run their action.

ListSubheader titles groups (an <li> by default). inset aligns the title with the text of rows that have an icon; sticky pins it while the list scrolls. You can also pass it through the subheader prop of List.
dense on the list reduces the vertical padding of its rows (also nested ones) from 8px to 4px.

A List with nested inside a row indents its rows by 48px ( nested={2}: 72px) and shares the selection of the parent list. Wrap it in Collapse (exported by the package) to expand and collapse it; the parent row uses aria-expanded, aria-controls and disableSelect so it is not selected.

secondaryAction on ListItem renders the action in ListItemSecondaryAction: aligned to the end, it accepts several actions of any width and a trailing IconButton snaps to the edge. For a clickable row with a separate action, use a ListItem disablePadding with the ListItemButton as child and the action in secondaryAction.
Hover to see the hover state and use Tab for focus. disabled disables the row: the native disabled on buttons, aria-disabled="true" and tabIndex={-1} on links, and aria-disabled on static rows.
With href the rows are links; the selected one gets aria-current="page".

onSelect is the equivalent of the vanilla mtx:list:select event: it receives { item, value } (the row element and its value). The selected setter and disable() / enable() become the value prop of List (or selected on a row) and disabled.

For full control (the equivalent of the vanilla BEM syntax), compose ListItemIcon, ListItemAvatar, ListItemText and ListItemSecondaryAction inside the rows. When the children of a row are not plain text, they are rendered as is.

d: Displays data sets in rows and columns on a semantic HTML table, with density, sticky header, sorting, selection and pagination.

s.x: Table implements MUI’s table family on a semantic <table>: TableContainer, TableHead, TableBody, TableFooter, TableRow and TableCell, plus the interactive pieces TableSortLabel, TablePagination and TableToolbar. Row selection is data-driven with the useTableSelection hook and the existing Checkbox. Use it for multi-column data that users compare or scan. For a single column of items use List; for summary cards use Card.

TableContainer: <div class="mtx-table-container"> that scrolls horizontally (and vertically with maxHeight). Table: <table class="mtx-table">; shares size, padding, hover and selectable with its children through context. TableHead / TableBody / TableFooter: <thead>, <tbody> and <tfoot>. Cells inside TableHead render as <th scope="col">. TableRow / TableCell: <tr class="mtx-table-row"> and <th> / <td class="mtx-table-cell">. TableCaption: <caption class="mtx-table-caption">, shown below the table.
Right-align numeric columns with align="right" on the header and the body cells, or with numeric.
size="medium" (16px padding, default) or size="small" (6px vertical padding, mtx-table--small). A single TableCell also accepts size.
hover on Table highlights the body rows (header and footer rows are not affected); hover on a TableRow highlights only that row. selected adds mtx-table-row--selected and aria-selected="true".

stickyHeader on TableContainer (or Table) keeps the header visible and maxHeight (number in px or any CSS value) limits the height. While the container scrolls it becomes a focusable region ( tabindex="0", role="region") named by the caption, the table’s aria-labelledby / aria-label or a translated fallback; a ResizeObserver keeps it in sync, as in vanilla.

TableSortLabel is controlled: active and direction describe the current order and onSort(event, { direction, active, key }) reports the requested one (the equivalent of mtx:table:sort). The parent <th> gets aria-sort automatically. useTableSort() keeps a single active column and sortRows + getComparator sort the data with a stable sort. In right-aligned columns the arrow is placed on the left.

useTableSelection(rows, getId, options) reproduces vanilla’s data-selectable: the header checkbox selects every selectable, enabled row and turns indeterminate with a partial selection; rows get aria-selected; the selection is stored by id, so it survives sorting, filtering and pagination. isRowSelectable excludes a row ( data-no-select), isRowDisabled disables its checkbox and selectOnClick toggles a row when clicking outside its controls. By default the keys of rows that are no longer in rows are kept, so numSelected and the toolbar still count them. When rows is the whole data set and rows can be deleted (or reloaded from the server), pass pruneMissing: true to drop those keys automatically (it calls onSelectionChange with reason: 'api'). Do not use it when rows is only the filtered or current page, or the selection would be lost on filtering or paging.

TableToolbar (MUI’s EnhancedTableToolbar) shows the title and the actions with no selection; with numSelected > 0 it is highlighted, announces the count in a live region and shows the selectedActions.

TablePagination renders the native rows-per-page select, the displayed range (live region) and the navigation buttons. It can be controlled ( page, rowsPerPage) or uncontrolled ( defaultPage, defaultRowsPerPage); -1 in rowsPerPageOptions means “All” and count={-1} an unknown total. Slice the data with paginateRows(rows, page, rowsPerPage).
