d: Short informative label shown on hover, keyboard focus or long press. Wrap any element with <Tooltip title>.

s.x: A Tooltip shows a short text label that identifies or explains an element when the user hovers over it, focuses it with the keyboard or long-presses it on a touch screen, just like MUI’s Tooltip. It is ideal for icon-only buttons and toolbars. Do not put essential information or interactive content in it (links, buttons): for persistent messages use a helper text or an Alert.

Wrap a single child with <Tooltip title="…">. The child receives the merged ref and chained pointer and focus handlers, so it must be an element or a component that forwards them (every Materix component does). If the child has no accessible name (an icon-only IconButton), the title becomes its aria-label.
placement accepts 12 positions ( top|bottom|left|right with -start|-end); the default is bottom. If it doesn’t fit, it flips to the opposite side and shifts to stay on screen.
arrow adds an arrow that points at the center of the trigger, even when the tooltip shifts to fit.
It works on text buttons, buttons with a start or end icon and, above all, on icon-only buttons such as IconButton and Fab, where it also provides the accessible name.

Disabled elements don’t receive pointer or focus events: wrap them with a <span> so the tooltip can still explain why they are unavailable, as MUI recommends. The accessible name is applied to the first focusable element inside the wrapper.
By default it appears after 100 ms ( enterDelay) and disappears on leave ( leaveDelay 0). After one closes, the next one opens with enterNextDelay (0 ms) for 800 ms, ideal for toolbars.
followCursor anchors the tooltip to the pointer while it moves over the trigger. Such a tooltip cannot be reached by the pointer, so it does not retain it (as with disableInteractive).
The maximum width is 300 px ( --mtx-tooltip-max-width) and the text wraps onto several lines.

title accepts any ReactNode (formatting, keyboard shortcuts). Keep it non-interactive. With a non-text title, an unnamed trigger is labelled with aria-labelledby while the tooltip is visible; describeChild turns it into a description.
If the trigger has no accessible name, the text is applied as aria-label. If it already has one, the tooltip describes it with aria-describedby while visible.
An editor’s formatting bar with keyboard shortcuts (instant opening as you move across the buttons) and extra information next to a value.
Tooltips are portaled to <body>: containers with overflow or narrow columns of a Grid don’t clip them.

open makes the tooltip controlled: onOpen(event) and onClose(event) ask to change it (equivalents of mtx:tooltip:open and mtx:tooltip:close). For one-off actions without state, the action ref exposes open(), close(), toggle(), update() and isOpen, the equivalent of Materix.tooltip.show/hide and getTooltip(). hideAllTooltips() hides every visible tooltip.

d: A short, prominent message that reports the outcome of an action or the state of the system without interrupting the user.

s.x: Alert shows a short, important message inside the page flow, with a color and an icon that communicate its severity ( success, info, warning, error). Use it to confirm an operation, warn about a problem or explain a validation error next to the affected content. Don’t use it for temporary notifications that disappear on their own (use a Snackbar) or for decisions that block the task (use a Dialog).
<Alert severity="…"> is enough: the component renders the severity icon, the.mtx-alert__message container and, with title, the title.

Three variants, as in MUI: standard (soft background, default), filled (solid background) and outlined (border only). standard and outlined use the severity color darkened in the light theme and lightened in the dark theme, so the text keeps its contrast.
By default the severity SVG icon is rendered at 22px, as in MUI. icon replaces it (a node, or a Material Icons name, which keeps its 24px grid) and icon={false} removes it.
severity sets the color and the icon. Use success, info, warning or error according to the meaning of the message; without the prop, success is applied.
title renders a bold.mtx-alert__title above the message. You can also write <AlertTitle> as the first child, as in MUI.
action places content to the right of the message (for example, an “Undo” button).

onClose (or dismissible) adds an accessible close button; closeLabel changes its label for screen readers (by default, Close / Cerrar from the i18n dictionary). When closed, the alert fades out for 200 ms, receives hidden (it leaves the flow: no gap is left) and calls onClosed. Uncontrolled alerts close by themselves; with open, onClose is a request and you update the state.

Bind open to the validation result (the fields are outlined TextField s): a closed alert has hidden and takes no space. Submit the empty form to see the error and fill it in to see the success message.
Alerts take the width of their container, so they fit any grid column.
The equivalent of close() / open() is the open prop. onOpen and onClosed are the equivalents of the mtx:alert:open and mtx:alert:close events; new alerts are just rendered.

d: Full-screen layer that dims the page and centers an indicator while an operation runs; it does not replace a dialog.

s.x: Backdrop covers the whole screen with a semi-transparent layer and centers its content, usually a CircularProgress. Use it to signal that the page is busy during a short operation (saving, syncing, processing a payment). It is not a dialog: it has no role, doesn’t trap focus and offers no title or actions; if the user must read a message or make a decision, use a Dialog, which already includes its own backdrop (it reuses this component).

<Backdrop open={…}> with the content to center. open is controlled: onClose asks to close it and you update the state. With closeOnClick a click on the layer closes it, and with closeOnEscape, the Escape key. The content is white by default, so a CircularProgress color="inherit" stands out in both themes.

Two variants, as in MUI: the default one dims the page with --mtx-backdrop-bg, and invisible keeps the layer transparent (it still blocks clicks). With invisible the content keeps the text color, so use a colored indicator.
Children are centered with flexbox; combine them with Stack and Typography. Any element marked with data-mtx-backdrop-close closes the layer (reason click), even without closeOnClick.

closeOnClick: a click on the layer or on non-interactive content asks to close (reason click). Clicks on buttons, links or fields inside the content are ignored. closeOnEscape: Escape asks to close (reason escape) through the shared layer stack, so it only reaches the top layer. Without either flag the layer only closes when you set open={false} (for example, when the operation ends).

lockScroll locks the <body> scroll while it is open (modal manager shared with Dialog), and inertOthers marks the rest of the document as inert (no focus, no clicks, hidden from screen readers) and restores it on close. With either of them the backdrop joins the layer stack and consumes Escape even if it doesn’t close with it.
Saving a form: the backdrop covers the page while the request runs and closes by itself when it finishes; then a Snackbar confirms the result. The project name is a TextField.
The layer is rendered in a portal on document.body and does not take part in the layout; here a grid of triggers opens the same backdrop with different messages.

The equivalent of open() / close() / toggle() is the open prop. onOpen and onClose(event, reason) are the equivalents of mtx:backdrop:open and mtx:backdrop:close; onExited fires when the fade-out ends.

d: A modal window that interrupts the task to ask for a decision or show critical information, with trapped focus and Escape to close.

s.x: Dialog opens a modal panel over the page: it locks scrolling, traps keyboard focus and requires a decision before continuing. Use it for confirmations, short forms or information the user must not miss. Don’t use it for notices that need no response (use Snackbar or Alert) or for side navigation (use a Drawer).

The simplest form is a single element: <Dialog open={…} onClose={…} title="…"> with the content as children. open is controlled: onClose(event, reason) asks to close it and you update the state. The dialog is rendered in a portal on document.body, with the shared Backdrop as its background; Escape and a click on the backdrop close it.

With scroll="paper" (default) the content scrolls inside the panel; DialogContent dividers separates the areas and DialogTitle sticky / DialogActions sticky pin the title and the actions. With scroll="body" the panel grows with its content and the dialog container is what scrolls.

By default the dialog closes with a click on the backdrop ( backdropClick) and with Escape ( escapeKeyDown). disableBackdropClose and disableEscapeKeyDown force the user to choose an explicit action (Escape is still consumed by the dialog, so it doesn’t reach the layers below). While it is open, page scrolling is locked ( disableScrollLock turns it off).

Dialogs join the shared layer stack: a dialog opened from another one is stacked above it (its z-index rises automatically), focus is trapped only in the top one, and each Escape closes only the top layer.

A Popover, a Menu and a Tooltip opened inside a dialog join the same layer stack: each Escape closes only the top layer (a visible tooltip first), focus moves into them without being pulled back to the panel, and interacting with them never closes the dialog.
Inside the content you can use Grid for multi-column forms; combine it with maxWidth="lg" to give the columns room.

For full control, compose the parts: DialogTitle names the dialog ( aria-labelledby) and the first DialogContentText describes it ( aria-describedby); the ids are generated from the dialog id (or a unique id). You can mix both forms: title and actions are still added when you use DialogContent as a child.

s.x: Progress tells the user that an operation is running. CircularProgress fits small spaces (buttons, cards, a loading page) and LinearProgress is placed at the edge of a container or next to the task it measures. Use the indeterminate variant when the remaining time is unknown and determinate when you know the percentage.
A single <CircularProgress /> or <LinearProgress /> renders the SVG or the bars, role="progressbar" and the accessible name. Without value it is indeterminate; with value it becomes determinate.

As in MUI: indeterminate (spins with a stroke that grows and shrinks), determinate (an arc proportional to value) and disableShrink (spin only, useful when the main thread is very busy). track adds the background ring.
Four variants: indeterminate, determinate, buffer (inferred from valueBuffer) and query (reversed indeterminate, for the phase before loading starts). 4px high, as in MUI; rounded rounds the ends.
size sets the diameter in px (40 by default) and thickness the stroke width (3.6). The height of the linear bar is changed with the --mtx-linear-progress-height variable.
showLabel shows the rounded percentage: centered in the circle and to the right of the bar. The visual figure is aria-hidden; screen readers get the value from aria-valuenow.
color accepts the palette colors and inherit (takes the container’s text color). The linear track is lightened in the light theme and darkened in the dark theme.

min and max change the scale (0–100 by default): <LinearProgress max={10} value={7} /> exposes aria-valuemax="10" and fills 70%. If max <= min, max becomes min + 100. The value is clamped to the range.

The default accessible name is “Loading” / “Cargando” depending on the language ( I18nProvider, <html lang> or the locale prop). Customize it with label, aria-label or aria-labelledby. Mark the region being updated with aria-busy="true" while it loads.
File upload with value and buffer, seat and storage usage on a custom scale, and a Button with loading, which uses a decorative CircularProgress inside.
The linear bar fills the width of its column; the circular indicator is centered with flex.
Progress is a controlled component: update value, valueBuffer, color or variant from your state. Passing value={undefined} switches back to indeterminate.

d: Content-shaped placeholders shown while data loads, with a pulse or wave animation.

s.x: Skeleton displays a grey block shaped like content that hasn’t arrived yet (text, avatar, image, card). It reduces perceived waiting and avoids layout shifts when the data appears. Use it for short loads of content with a known structure; if you don’t know what shape the result will have, or the operation doesn’t load content (saving, sending), use Progress.
Without a variant, <Skeleton /> is a line of text that fills the available width and takes the height of the typography. width and height accept numbers (px) or any CSS unit.
Four shapes, as in MUI: text (default, scaled down to 60% of the line height), circular, rectangular (no radius) and rounded (4px radius).
animation="pulse" (default), "wave" or false (static; the string "false" is accepted too). With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the animation is turned off automatically.
The text variant inherits the size of the typography it sits in: place it inside the same element that will hold the real text. Circular shapes follow the canonical Avatar sizes (24, 40 and 56px).
lines={3} generates a.mtx-skeleton-lines block with several lines of text; the last one is shorter (60% by default, configurable with lastWidth). With lines, variant and height have no effect.

When the skeleton wraps content, it takes its exact size and hides it ( visibility: hidden, class.mtx-skeleton--with-children). Direct text is wrapped in.mtx-skeleton__text so it is hidden too instead of being transparent text that fails contrast checks.

SkeletonRegion is the React equivalent of Materix.skeleton.set(). While loading is true it renders data-loading and aria-busy="true" on the root, shows the placeholder (inside [data-skeleton-placeholder], always aria-hidden) and hides the children (inside [data-skeleton-content]). Both wrappers stay mounted and the CSS hides the inactive one, so the content keeps its state. With aria-live="polite" the content is announced when loading finishes. Use placeholderProps and contentProps to style the wrappers. If you prefer to unmount the content while loading, the MUI pattern also works: loading? <Skeleton />: <Content />.
A video card and a message list while loading.
Blocks without a fixed width fill their column.
variant and animation are ordinary props (they replace setVariant() and setAnimation()); SkeletonRegion calls onChange({ loading }) whenever loading changes after mounting.

d: Brief, temporary notification at an edge of the screen that confirms an action and can offer to undo it.

s.x: Snackbar shows a short floating message at an edge of the screen to confirm the outcome of an action (“Email sent”, “Item deleted”) and, optionally, offer a single action such as “Undo”. It does not interrupt the user and can close on its own. Do not use it for errors the user must resolve (use an Alert next to the content) or for mandatory decisions (use a Dialog).

<Snackbar open={…} message="…"> is enough. open is controlled: onClose(event, reason) asks to close it and you update the state. It closes with Escape, on a click outside or, with autoHideDuration, when the time runs out.

A text action renders the.mtx-snackbar__action button on the right; onAction runs when it is pressed and closeOnAction closes the snackbar (reason action). Any other node (for example an IconButton) is rendered as is.
anchorOrigin combines vertical ( top / bottom) with horizontal ( left / center / right); by default, bottom center. Below 600px the snackbar spans the full width with an 8px side margin.
Without autoHideDuration (or with null) the snackbar does not close by itself. The timer pauses while the pointer or focus is on it and restarts with the full duration when they leave.
SnackbarProvider keeps a queue and shows one notice at a time: a new notice closes the visible one and appears when its exit transition ends, as in MUI’s Consecutive Snackbars example.

For notifications with a severity, place an Alert as the child of a snackbar without message. The mtx-p-0 mtx-bg-transparent utilities remove the snackbar padding and background, and mtx-flex-1 stretches the alert.

For one-off confirmations you don’t need to declare a snackbar: wrap the app once with <SnackbarProvider> and call useSnackbar().enqueue(message | options). The shared snackbar uses role="status" and a 4 s duration by default; onAction runs when the action is pressed and closes the notice. enqueue returns a key that close(key) accepts.
A subscription form with an Email TextField: when the address is valid, the shared snackbar confirms it and offers to undo it.
A typical case: actions in a Grid where each one confirms its result with the shared snackbar.

Escape only closes the most recent snackbar, and never while a dialog or menu is open on top.

d: Panels that show and hide related sections of content behind a clickable summary, ideal for FAQs and grouped settings.

s.x: Accordion organizes content into collapsible panels: a clickable summary (AccordionSummary) shows or hides the details (AccordionDetails) with a height transition. Use it for FAQs, sectioned settings or secondary information that shouldn’t take up space permanently. Don’t use it for primary navigation (use Tabs or a Drawer) or to hide content users always need to see.

The simplest form: the summary prop is the summary text and the children become the details (the equivalent of the vanilla single-element syntax with data-summary). It renders the <h3> heading, the <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls, the expand_more icon and the collapsible region. Adjacent panels share 1px separators and only the first and last ones get rounded corners.

component="details" renders a native <details> / <summary>: with server rendering it works even before React hydrates. The panel keeps the MUI look, the height animation and the icon; defaultExpanded sets open, and the browser’s find-in-page (Ctrl+F) opens the panel that contains the match (reported through onChange). A <summary> can’t live inside a heading, so the details form doesn’t generate an <h3>. If the heading outline matters for your page, use the default div form.
By default the accordion is a Paper surface with elevation 1. variant="outlined" uses a 1px border (adjacent borders are merged), elevation={0} makes it flat and square removes the rounded corners.

By default the summary uses medium weight (500) and, while the panel is expanded, an --mtx-color-action-selected background plus a bottom divider, also in the outlined variant. Focus ( --mtx-color-action-focus) takes precedence over that background. summaryStyle="plain" (on the panel or on the group) restores MUI’s flat look: regular weight, no background and no divider. Tune it with the --mtx-accordion-summary-* CSS variables. Deliberate deviation from MUI MUI’s AccordionSummary uses regular weight and the same background as the details. Materix emphasizes the summary by default so an open panel’s heading is easy to tell from its content. Use summaryStyle="plain" for the original MUI look.
When expanded, the panel gets a 16px vertical margin and the summary grows from 48px to 64px. disableGutters keeps the 48px height and removes the margin.

The expand icon is expand_more and rotates 180° when opened. expandIcon accepts a Material Icons name or any node (for example an SVG), and expandIcon={false} omits it. The rotation angle is set with the --mtx-accordion-expand-icon-rotation variable (for example 45deg for an add icon). The summary prop also accepts nodes, such as a leading icon.

Keyboard focus paints the summary with the action.focus background, like MUI. disabled dims the summary to 38%, applies the disabled background and blocks interaction. As in MUI, the summary has no ripple by default; ripple enables it. duration fixes the collapse time in milliseconds ( 'auto', the default, derives it from the height with the MUI formula; 0 disables the animation).

AccordionGroup keeps a single panel open (MUI’s “Controlled accordion” pattern) and enables arrow, Home and End navigation between summaries. With exclusive={false} several panels can be open. The group passes variant, elevation, square, disableGutters and summaryStyle down to the panels that don’t set them. When several panels start with defaultExpanded in an exclusive group, only the first one stays open.
An AccordionActions child is placed at the bottom of the region, after the details, right-aligned with 8px between buttons. disableSpacing removes that spacing.
An FAQ built with component="details" inside an exclusive group, and settings whose summary carries secondary text ( AccordionSummary with secondary, as in MUI’s “Controlled accordion” demo).

The vanilla expand(), collapse(), toggle() and expanded setter become the controlled expanded prop plus onChange, which replaces the mtx:accordion:change event. The AccordionGroup methods expandAll() and collapseAll() are available through actionRef.

For full control (the equivalent of the vanilla BEM syntax), compose AccordionSummary, AccordionDetails and AccordionActions. If there is no AccordionDetails, the remaining children are wrapped in one; actions always go after the details.

d: Top bar with the title, navigation and primary actions of the current screen.

s.x: AppBar is the application’s top bar: it displays the screen title, the navigation button and the most frequent actions inside a Toolbar. Use it once per screen as a header. To switch between views at the same level use Tabs, for primary navigation combine it with a Drawer, and for a floating primary action use a Fab.

title, startIcon and endIcon generate the Toolbar, the title and the IconButtons (the equivalent of the vanilla single-element syntax). Any children are placed after the title. The bar is fixed by default; these demos use position="static" so it stays inside the page.

color accepts primary, secondary, default (paper surface; the default value), transparent and inherit. elevation changes the shadow (4 by default); it is written to the --mtx-app-bar-shadow variable so transparent and --flat can cancel it. With elevation={0} the bar gets mtx-app-bar--flat and, in default, a single bottom divider instead of the shadow.

The regular Toolbar is 56px tall on mobile and 64px from 600px up, with 16 and 24px side gutters. dense reduces it to 48px and toolbarVariant="prominent" raises it to 128px with the title at the bottom. disableGutters removes the side gutters.

startIcon adds the navigation button (.mtx-toolbar__navigation-icon) and endIcon a trailing action; both accept a Material Icons name or a node. Set their accessible names with startIconLabel and endIconLabel; without them, the menu icon (or any start icon with navigationControls) is labeled “Open navigation” from the i18n dictionary ( appBar.openNavigation) and other icons fall back to their name. For several actions write them as children and mark the title with ToolbarTitle. Inside the Toolbar, text and outlined Buttons and IconButtons inherit the bar color; contained buttons keep their own colors.

position defines how the bar behaves when the page scrolls. Value Behavior fixed (default) Fixed to the top of the viewport (app bar z-index). Start the content with <ToolbarOffset /> to reserve its height (56px, 64px from 600px; dense 48px). sticky Flows with the content and sticks to the top when it reaches it. static Part of the normal flow; scrolls with the page. absolute Anchored to the top of the positioned ancestor; with bottom, to the bottom. relative Relative position, no anchoring. clipped raises the z-index above a clipped Drawer. When the page has a fixed or sticky bar, the CSS adds scroll-padding-top to <html> so #anchor targets aren’t hidden under it (tune it with --mtx-scroll-padding-top). In the demo, the fixed bar is contained by a transform on its frame; on a real page it stays fixed to the window.

Actions open a Menu with useMenu() (the equivalent of vanilla data-open-menu). For search, use the.mtx-app-bar-search pattern (40px tall, with --grow, --right, --centered and --compact modifiers) or a TextField with variant="no-label" and size="small", which can shrink inside the Toolbar. Their fill, text and placeholder derive from the bar color, so they keep their contrast on primary, secondary, default and in the dark theme. Wrap the pattern with role="search" and give the input an aria-label.

elevateOnScroll starts without a shadow and applies the elevation on scroll; hideOnScroll hides the bar when scrolling down (past 50px) and shows it when scrolling up. The window is observed by default; scrollTarget accepts a ref, an element, a function or a CSS selector of the scrolling container. The calculation runs once per frame and the pending frame is canceled on unmount.

The Toolbar changes height and gutters at 600px. For navigation, show text links on wide screens and an icon with a Menu on narrow ones, toggling them with the mtx-d-md-none / mtx-d-md-flex utilities.

In vanilla, data-drawer="id" turns the navigation button into the trigger of a Drawer. In React, onNavigationClick opens the Drawer and navigationControls / navigationExpanded keep aria-controls and aria-expanded in sync. For the full app shell (fixed bar + responsive clipped Drawer + ToolbarOffset), see the Drawer page.
The bar takes 100% of its container width; the screen content is laid out below it with Grid.
The vanilla setColor() and setPosition() methods become the color and position props; any change is a re-render. The vanilla bar emits no events.
If the children include a Toolbar, no Toolbar is generated (the equivalent of the vanilla full BEM syntax): use it for several Toolbars, prominent bars or full control of the content.

The root is a <header>: it’s the banner landmark when it sits at the top level of the page. Generated IconButtons always have an aria-label ( startIconLabel / endIconLabel, the i18n “Open navigation” or the icon name) and their icons are aria-hidden. d: A surface that groups content and actions about a single subject: header, image, text and buttons.

s.x: Card groups the information and actions of a single item on an elevated surface: a product, a recipe, a profile. It is built from optional parts —header, media, content, actions and action area— that you can generate with shorthand props on Card or compose with subcomponents. Use it when the block is self-contained and scannable within a collection; for a generic surface without structure use Paper, and for dense lists use List.

title, subheader, avatar, actionIcon and image generate the header and the image (the equivalent of the vanilla single-element syntax); the content and actions are children: CardContent and CardActions.

By default the card has elevation 1. variant="outlined" delimits it with a border and no shadow; raised raises it to 8 (like MUI’s raised); elevation accepts 0–8, 12, 16 and 24; square removes the radius. The h1 – h6 and p styles inside CardContent have zero specificity, so Typography (or any mtx-typography--* class) always wins.

The header (.mtx-card__header) is generated when there is a title, subheader or avatar. A string avatar is painted as a primary Avatar with that text; any other node (for example an <Avatar>) is rendered as is. actionIcon adds an IconButton on the right (its name comes from actionLabel, default “Actions”), and action accepts any node instead.

image generates a full-bleed 194 px CardMedia. By default it goes after the header; mediaTop places it at the top and mediaHeight sets the height. A generated image is decorative ( aria-hidden) unless you pass imageAlt.

CardActions is a row with 8 px of padding and gap; its buttons take MUI’s compact size and are right-aligned by default (see Actions alignment). The mtx-card__actions-end class pushes one item to the far right, and disableSpacing removes the gap.

Card actions are right-aligned by default, like dialog actions. Change it with align="start|center|end|between" on CardActions, or for every action row of a card with actionsAlign on Card (a row’s own align wins). Deliberate deviation from MUI MUI’s CardActions aligns its buttons to the left. Materix aligns them to the right by default so that cards and dialogs share the same action placement. Use align="start" (or actionsAlign="start" on the card) to get the original MUI layout.

CardActionArea turns the image and text into a single clickable zone with ripple, hover and focus, without affecting the actions. It renders a <button type="button">, an <a> when it receives href, or any element through component (then it gets role="button", tabIndex={0} and Enter/Space). With clickable the whole card becomes interactive ( role="button", ripple, Enter and Space).

Normal, hover and focus (hover or use Tab) and disabled. disabled on a clickable card or on CardActionArea lowers the opacity, removes the pointer and takes it out of the tab order ( aria-disabled="true"; on a <button> also the native disabled).

In dark mode, as in MUI, each elevation adds a white overlay ( --mtx-overlay-elevation-N): elevation 0 has no overlay, the card raised to 8 looks lighter than the elevation 1 card, and outlined has no overlay.
Cards take the width of their column, so they adapt to any grid.

The vanilla methods become props and refs: disabled replaces disable() / enable(), ref.current.focus() replaces focus() and the image prop of CardMedia replaces its setter. There are no mtx:* events: use onClick (also fired by Enter and Space on non-native elements).

For full control (the equivalent of the vanilla BEM syntax), compose CardHeader, CardMedia, CardContent and CardActions yourself. Every part accepts className, style, native attributes and ref; Card, CardHeader, CardMedia and CardContent also accept component.

d: The base Material Design surface, with background, border radius and shadow, that groups content and expresses elevation.

s.x: Paper is the physical surface of Material Design: a container with a paper background, a 4px border radius and a shadow that conveys its elevation. It is the visual foundation of Card, Dialog, Menu and AppBar. Use it to group arbitrary content on top of the page background; if the block has a header, an image and actions, use a Card directly.
<Paper> renders a <div class="mtx-paper"> with elevation 1. Change the shadow with elevation.
The default variant ( elevation) sets the surface apart with a shadow. variant="outlined" outlines it with a 1px border ( --mtx-color-divider) and no shadow; elevation={0} makes it flat.

Only MUI elevations 0 to 8, 12, 16 and 24 exist as tokens ( --mtx-elevation-*). Any other value generates an unstyled class and the surface keeps the base elevation 1. Typical use (MUI) Elevation Card at rest, base Paper 1 AppBar 4 Raised Card, Menu 8 Drawer 16 Dialog 24
Corners use --mtx-shape-radius (4px). square makes them straight, which is useful for surfaces flush with the edges of the viewport.

Paper consumes --mtx-color-background-paper and --mtx-color-text-primary, so it follows the theme. data-mtx-theme="dark" also works on a specific container. In the dark theme, as in MUI, each elevation adds a white overlay ( --mtx-overlay-elevation-N) through background-image, so higher surfaces look lighter; outlined has no overlay.
Paper is the usual container for grid items: the column sets the width and Paper provides the surface.
There is nothing to initialize: elevation, variant and square are ordinary props, so changing them updates the classes on the next render.
component changes the root tag ( section, article, aside …) without changing the look. Combine it with Typography for the content.

d: Floating Paper with arbitrary content anchored to a trigger. Closes on click away or Escape and returns focus to the trigger.

s.x: A Popover displays any content (text, forms, cards) on a floating Paper surface anchored to another element, like MUI’s Popover. Use it for filters, quick details, small confirmations or an account card. For a list of actions use a Menu; for a short text label, a Tooltip; for a task that blocks the page, a Dialog. It is also the floating base other components build on (date pickers, filter panels): it handles positioning, the layer stack, focus and closing.

usePopover() is the equivalent of data-open-popover="#id": spread getTriggerProps() on the trigger and popoverProps on the <Popover>. It opens below the trigger aligned to its start edge, with elevation 8. Focus moves to the first control (or to the panel) and returns to the trigger when it closes. The panel is rendered in a portal on document.body, so ancestors with overflow: hidden or their own z-index never clip it. Content padding is up to you: use utilities such as mtx-p-2.
placement uses the same engine as Tooltip ( top|bottom|left|right with -start|-end; default bottom-start), with automatic flipping and shifting. offset sets the gap in px (0 by default, as in MUI).

MUI’s API: anchorOrigin={{ vertical, horizontal }} is the point on the anchor and transformOrigin the point on the popover attached to it. Values are top|center|bottom and left|center|right, or pixels (numbers). The popover stays marginThreshold px (16) from the viewport edges and the grow animation starts from the transform origin. When either origin is set it takes precedence over placement.

Any button can be the trigger. Icon-only ones need an accessible name ( aria-label). The trigger gets aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-controls and a synchronized aria-expanded. Several triggers can share one popover: give each one a key ( getTriggerProps({ key })) so only the active one is expanded, and each trigger becomes the anchor when clicked. The heading inside the popover becomes its name automatically ( aria-labelledby).
A disabled trigger does not open the popover. Elements with data-mtx-popover-close inside the popover close it (reason action) and return focus.

anchorReference="anchorPosition" with anchorPosition={{ top, left }} anchors the popover to a viewport point instead of an element, for example the cursor position in a contextmenu event. usePopover().openPopover({ x, y }) does the same. With anchorReference="none" the popover is centered in the viewport.

By default the popover is non-modal: it does not trap focus or lock scrolling, and tabbing out of it closes it (reason tabOut). With modal it traps Tab, locks page scrolling and sets aria-modal="true", like MUI’s Popover; a click outside still closes it (reason clickaway) and reaches the clicked element, as in vanilla. data-autofocus on a control chooses the initial focus.

A button inside the popover can open a Dialog. Interacting with the dialog is not a “click outside” for the popover, the first Escape closes only the dialog (focus returns to the button inside the popover) and the second one closes the popover.

A popover can also open another popover (or a menu). Both share the layer stack: interacting with the upper layer is not a “click outside” for the popover, the first Escape closes only the upper layer (focus returns to its trigger inside the popover) and the second one closes the popover.

The popover is portaled to <body>, so columns and containers with overflow never clip it.

MUI’s hover pattern: open on mouseenter / focus, close on mouseleave / blur, with disableAutoFocus, disableRestoreFocus and the mtx-pointer-events-none utility so the popover never steals the pointer or the focus.

The open prop is the equivalent of open() / close(). usePopover() exposes openPopover(anchor), close() and toggle(anchor); onOpen and onClose(event, reason) are the equivalents of mtx:popover:open and mtx:popover:close. The action ref exposes updatePosition() (vanilla’s update()).

Popover is designed as the floating base for other surfaces. The props they rely on: resolveOrigin() (MUI origin to pixels) and the constants POPOVER_MARGIN_THRESHOLD and POPOVER_EXIT_DURATION are also exported.

d: Hierarchical navigation trail that shows where the user is and lets them jump back to any parent level.

s.x: Breadcrumbs renders the path from the root of the site or app to the current page, like MUI’s Breadcrumbs: a <nav> with an ordered list, separators hidden from assistive technologies and the last item marked with aria-current="page". Use it in hierarchies of three or more levels (catalogs, documentation, file managers). Do not use it as primary navigation or for linear flows.

Pass Links and the current page as children. Each child goes into an <li>, links get color="inherit" and underline on hover (unless they set their own), plain text becomes a <span class="mtx-breadcrumbs__text">, and the last item is marked as the current page. Native <a> and <button> children are converted into Links.
If the last item must stay a link, set aria-current="page" yourself: the component respects it and does not mark any other item.

separator accepts any text (default /), any node, or the name of a Material icon: a string made of lowercase letters, digits and underscores, with three or more characters ( navigate_next, chevron_right), is rendered as an icon.
data-icon on a child (or icon in items) adds a decorative Material icon before the label. As in MUI, the icon sits outside the text flow: only the label is underlined on hover.

When there are more items than maxItems (8 by default), only itemsBeforeCollapse (1) and itemsAfterCollapse (1) are shown, separated by a “Show path” button. Activating it reveals the hidden items, moves focus to the first one and calls onExpand. The trail collapses again when its items change.
Like MUI, it uses body1 in text.secondary and the current page in text.primary. For a more compact trail, use variant="body2" (it adds the Typography class mtx-typography--body2).
Links keep the Link states (underline on hover, focus ring with Tab). A trail link can be disabled with disabled, and its own color changes it.

items describes the trail as data ( { label, href?, icon?, current?, disabled?, data? }), equivalent to vanilla’s setItems(). Items with href are Links; the current page (the last one, unless an item sets current) is text; the rest are Links on a <button>. data becomes data-* attributes.

d: Side panel for navigation or supplementary content: temporary, persistent, permanent or responsive, with a generated header and footer and an app shell pattern.

s.x: Drawer is a panel that slides in from an edge of the screen to show the app’s navigation or supplementary content (filters, details, options), like MUI’s Drawer. Use it for primary navigation on mobile (temporary) or as a fixed sidebar on desktop (permanent). For a decision or a short form that interrupts the flow use a Dialog; for a short list of actions on an item, a Menu.

<Drawer open={…} onClose={…} title="…"> with the content directly inside. title generates the header with a title and a close button; the content is wrapped in the scrollable panel.mtx-drawer__content, and the temporary drawer adds a Backdrop. open is controlled: onClose(event, reason) asks to close and you update the state.

The main recipe for an application: an AppBar, a row with a variant="responsive" drawer (temporary below breakpoint, permanent above it) and the main content. The AppBar connects to the drawer through its navigation button, the React equivalent of vanilla’s data-drawer="id": navigationControls={drawerId} sets aria-controls on the menu button, navigationExpanded={open} keeps aria-expanded in sync, onNavigationClick toggles the state, useDrawerMode('responsive', 'md') returns the current mode, so startIcon={mode === 'temporary'? 'menu': undefined} hides the button while the drawer is permanent (vanilla adds.mtx-drawer-trigger--hidden). The drawer ignores clicks on its own trigger (any element with aria-controls pointing to its id), so the toggle doesn’t close and reopen it. Here the shell lives inside a frame ( absolute); on a full page use clipped and a ToolbarOffset at the top of <main>.

temporary (default): modal over a backdrop. It locks the page scroll, traps focus, closes with Escape, the backdrop or a click outside, and is rendered in a portal on document.body. persistent: opens without a backdrop and the page stays usable; move the content yourself to make room for it. permanent: always visible, a fixed-width box in a flex row with a sticky panel of window height. It never asks to close. responsive: see “Responsive”. With absolute the drawer and its backdrop stay inside the positioned parent (no scroll lock), and the permanent drawer takes the container height.

Responsive default: min(85vw, 320px) on mobile, 280px from 600px and 300px from 900px. width="narrow" | "wide" | "full" sets 200px, 360px or 100vw; any number (px) or CSS length ( "40vw") is applied as is and also written to --mtx-drawer-width. It never exceeds 85% of the window except with full.

anchor="left" | "right" | "top" | "bottom". right is usually used for details or filters; top and bottom take the full width and fit their content (bottom sheet). Any element with data-mtx-drawer-close inside the drawer asks to close with reason closeButtonClick.

Without a title the drawer only wraps the content (give it an aria-label). title and subtitle generate a text header; userName, userEmail and userAvatar, a user header with an Avatar. footerInfo and footerAction (+ footerActionIcon, onFooterActionClick) create a fixed footer whose button also closes the drawer; the middle scrolls independently. closeButton={false} removes the X.

You can prevent implicit closing: disableBackdropClick (neither the backdrop nor a click outside closes it), disableEscapeKeyDown and hideBackdrop (no backdrop; a click outside still closes). The status line shows the reason received by onClose.

The AppBar spans the full width and the drawer starts below it. On a full page use clipped on a permanent, responsive or persistent drawer: it is placed at --mtx-app-bar-height (56px on mobile, 64px from 600px) and stacks under the AppBar (give the AppBar clipped too). The temporary drawer ignores clipped: it is modal and covers the AppBar, as in MUI. Inside a frame, as here, a permanent absolute drawer in the row under the AppBar achieves the same.

variant="responsive" with breakpoint="sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" (600, 900, 1200, 1536px; default md): below it the drawer is temporary and opens with its trigger; from it, permanent. When crossing the breakpoint, classes, ARIA, backdrop and focus are synced without animation, onModeChange(mode, previousMode) fires (vanilla mtx:drawer:mode-change), and an open temporary drawer asks to close with reason breakpoint so it doesn’t reappear when going back to mobile. If focus was inside when it becomes temporary, it moves to the visible trigger. The responsive drawer stays mounted and in place (no portal), so its content keeps its state. headerMode="temporary" shows the generated header only while it is temporary. Resize the window.

DrawerSubmenu is the equivalent of vanilla’s data-mtx-collapse-trigger +.mtx-collapse: a list item with aria-expanded and aria-controls, a.mtx-collapse-indicator that rotates 90°, and a nested List animated with Collapse. It works controlled ( open + onToggle) or uncontrolled ( defaultOpen). While collapsed its items are not focusable.

A right drawer with width="wide" and padded containing a form laid out with Grid and TextField. inputProps={{ 'data-drawer-autofocus': '' }} gives the search field the initial focus (prefer it to autoFocus, which would steal the focus before the drawer records the trigger to return to). Buttons with data-mtx-drawer-close close it.

With DrawerHeader, DrawerContent and DrawerFooter as children the drawer generates nothing: it places the header and footer outside the scrollable panel and adds the dialog semantics to DrawerContent. Name the panel with aria-labelledby (or aria-label) on the drawer.

d: MUI-styled text link on a native <a>: palette colors and three underline modes, without losing semantics.

s.x: Link applies MUI’s link style (primary color, always underlined by default) to a native <a>, to a <button> for actions that don’t navigate, or to your router’s link component. It inherits the typography of the surrounding text.
<Link href="…"> renders an <a class="mtx-link">. With no other props it uses the primary color and is always underlined (MUI v5 default), so it never relies on color alone.

The link’s variant is its underline: underline="always|hover|none". always is the default: a soft underline (40% of the color) that becomes solid on hover. Use hover or none only for links outside running text (navigation, lists, footers).
color accepts the six palette colors, the text colors ( text-primary, text-secondary) and inherit, which takes the color of the surrounding text (here, inside an Alert).

Hover to see the underline and use Tab to see the focus ring. disabled disables the link: on <a> it sets aria-disabled="true", removes it from the tab order and cancels clicks; on <button> it uses the native disabled attribute.

For actions that don’t navigate but should look like a link inside text, use component="button" (no native background, border or padding, and the typography of the surrounding text). Without type, it gets type="button" so it doesn’t submit forms.
Inside running text keep the default underline ( always) so the link doesn’t rely on color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). The link inherits the paragraph’s typography, so it fits any variant.
With target="_blank" always add rel="noopener noreferrer" and announce the change of context in the visible text or in an aria-label that contains it.
Secondary links under a sign-in form and a breadcrumb trail.
Footer with columns of links in a Grid: one column on mobile, two on tablet and four on desktop.
Links are created from state (there are no methods). component renders the Link style on any component: React Router’s Link, Next.js Link, etc. Their props ( to, prefetch …) are forwarded.

d: Temporary list of options anchored to a trigger: icons, shortcuts, dividers, selection, checkable items, submenus, context menu and full keyboard navigation.

s.x: Menu displays a temporary list of actions or options on an elevated surface, anchored to the element that opens it, like MUI’s Menu (Popper + Paper + MenuList). Use it for contextual actions on an item (edit, duplicate, delete), account menus or compact toolbars. To pick a value in a form use a NativeSelect; for the app’s main navigation, use Tabs. Anatomy:.mtx-menu__popper (positioned in a portal) ›.mtx-menu__paper (elevation 8) ›.mtx-menu ( role="menu") ›.mtx-menu-item ( role="menuitem") with optional.mtx-menu-item__icon, text, shortcut and.mtx-menu-item__check /.mtx-menu-item__expand.

useMenu() is the equivalent of vanilla’s data-open-menu: spread triggerProps on the trigger and menuProps on the Menu. The trigger toggles the menu and gets aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and aria-controls. The menu closes when an option is chosen, on a click outside, with Escape or with Tab.

Without useMenu, the menu is fully controlled, as in MUI: open, anchorEl and onClose. A single Menu can serve every row of a list: each button stores itself as anchorEl, so rows added later work too (vanilla needed click delegation for that).
Items have a minimum height of 48px; with dense (on the Menu or on each MenuItem), 32px. disableGutters removes the side padding.
icon inserts the icon before the text: a Material Icons name ( icon="edit") or any node (an SVG). Give icon-only triggers an aria-label.
<MenuDivider /> or <MenuItem divider /> (the equivalent of data-divider) render a role="separator" that the keyboard skips.
selected highlights the current option and receives focus when the menu is opened with the keyboard; disabled adds aria-disabled="true" and removes it from the navigation.

role="menuitemcheckbox" toggles aria-checked on click ( checked + onCheckedChange, or defaultChecked). role="menuitemradio" items inside a MenuGroup with value / defaultValue behave as a single choice; onSelect also receives the new checked state. The check mark only shows on checked options.
shortcut aligns a keyboard shortcut or metadata at the end; secondary adds a second line under the text; image shows a 24px picture instead of an icon.

The menu opens below the anchor, aligned to its start edge ( placement="bottom-start"); if there is no room it flips upwards, and while the page scrolls it keeps the chosen side ( lockSide). The height is limited to the available space and, in RTL, the alignment is mirrored. matchWidth matches the anchor width; anchorEl can be any element, a ref or a virtual anchor. If the anchor leaves the viewport the menu asks to close with anchorHidden.
With many options the content scrolls inside the paper. Type a letter to jump to the next option starting with it.

<Submenu label icon> renders an item with aria-haspopup="menu" and a chevron that opens a nested menu next to it: on hover (after 100 ms), on click, or with →, Enter or Space. Hovering another item closes it after 50 ms; ← or Escape close it and return focus to its item. Choosing an option closes the whole chain and reaches the root onSelect. In RTL it opens to the left, the chevron is mirrored and the arrow keys are swapped; if there is no room, it flips to the other side.

<ContextMenu target items> is the equivalent of Materix.Menu.createContextMenu(selector, items): target is an element, a ref or a CSS selector; each item accepts label, icon, image, shortcut, disabled, divider, action and submenu. It opens on right-click at the pointer position ( anchorPosition); with the Menu key or Shift + F10 it anchors to the area and focuses the first option. For your own markup, useContextMenu() returns onContextMenu and the props of a Menu.
Account menu in an App Bar, aligned to the end of the icon with placement="bottom-end".
Cards in a Grid with their own actions menu; the menu is rendered in a portal, so the card does not clip it.

The equivalent of open() / close() is the open prop. onOpen, onSelect(detail, event) and onClose(event, reason) are the equivalents of mtx:menu:open, mtx:menu:select and mtx:menu:close. restoreFocusTo chooses who receives focus when the menu closes.

Menu is made of a portal, a Grow transition, the paper and a MenuList. MenuList on its own (inside a Paper) keeps the keyboard navigation for always-visible menus. The split button of Button Group anchors a Menu to the whole group with matchWidth and returns focus to the arrow.

d: Lets users pick a page within a large set of results, with ellipsis, first/last buttons and a link mode for SSR.

s.x: Pagination implements MUI’s Pagination: page buttons with ellipsis computed by the same algorithm as usePagination, previous/next buttons and optional first/last buttons, text and outlined variants, circular and rounded shapes, three sizes and three colors. Use it to move through result lists, blog articles or catalogs.

count (total pages) is enough. The component renders the <nav> landmark, the list, the buttons, the ellipsis and the translated aria-label s. It is uncontrolled by default ( defaultPage, 1-based); use page + onChange to control it.
variant="text" (default) or outlined.
shape="circular" (default) or rounded (4px radius).
size="small" | "medium" | "large": 26px, 32px (default) and 40px items, like MUI’s PaginationItem.
color="standard" | "primary" | "secondary" sets the color of the selected page.
Show the first and last page buttons with showFirstButton and showLastButton; hide previous and next with hidePrevButton and hideNextButton.
siblingCount (1) sets how many pages are shown on each side of the current one, and boundaryCount (1) how many at the beginning and the end.

Items have hover, focus-visible ( Tab) and ripple on press ( disableRipple turns it off). Previous/next are disabled automatically at the ends; disabled disables the whole component. If the focused button becomes disabled (for example “next” on the last page), focus moves to the current page.

With getItemHref(page) every item is an <a href>: it works with server-side rendering, can open in a new tab and needs no JavaScript to navigate. Items that cannot navigate get aria-disabled="true" and no href. Cancelable navigation In link mode, clicking a page calls onChange(event, page) before navigating. If you call event.preventDefault(), the native navigation is cancelled and the page changes in the client (useful to load the results with fetch while keeping the links for crawlers). This is the equivalent of the cancelable mtx:pagination:change event in vanilla.
Client-side paginated article list built with List inside a Paper.

In controlled mode the parent owns page, so it can be changed from outside (buttons, URL, store). usePagination exposes the same logic as MUI’s hook to build your own UI: it returns items ( { type, page, selected, disabled, onClick }), page and goTo.

d: Tabs to switch between views at the same level, with an animated indicator, icons, vertical orientation and full keyboard navigation.

s.x: Tabs organizes related content into views at the same level and lets users switch between them without leaving the page, with an indicator that slides under the active tab. Use it when there are between two and about seven sibling sections that users consult one at a time (profile, security, notifications). Don’t use it for sequential steps or to navigate between top-level pages.

TabContext shares the active value between Tabs and the TabPanel s: it generates the ids, links aria-controls / aria-labelledby and hides the inactive panels with hidden. Without defaultValue, the first enabled tab is active. TabsContainer is optional: it groups tabs and panels on an outlined surface (.mtx-tabs-container).

By default tabs have their natural width ( variant="standard"). variant="fullWidth" distributes the width among them and centered centers them. A Tab without value receives its index, so a bar without panels only needs <Tab label> children. TabsContainer adds a bordered surface; with borderless it only groups.
icon accepts a Material Icons name (rendered as a decorative <span class="material-icons mtx-tab__icon">) or your own node. iconPosition="start" (default) or "end". Icon-only tabs need an aria-label.
The active tab and the indicator use --mtx-color-primary; as in vanilla, there are no textColor / indicatorColor props. For another hue, redefine the token on a container.

A disabled tab is dimmed, does not respond to clicks and is skipped by the keyboard. Hover to see the hover background, press to see the ripple ( disableRipple turns it off) and use Tab to see the focus ring.

When the tabs don’t fit, the bar scrolls horizontally (touch, wheel or keyboard) and the indicator follows the active tab. The scrollbar is hidden and there are no arrow buttons (unlike MUI’s variant="scrollable").
orientation="vertical" stacks the tabs, places the indicator on the right and switches the arrow keys to ↑ / ↓. A row Stack places the panels next to the bar.

By default the arrow keys only move focus and the tab is activated with Enter or Space (manual activation, recommended by WAI-ARIA when loading a panel is expensive). With selectionFollowsFocus the tab is activated as soon as it receives focus.
Account settings with full-width tabs, icons and panels with controls.
Two groups inside a Grid: the indicator is recalculated when the width changes ( ResizeObserver and resize).

d: Floating action button that reveals three to six related, labeled actions in four directions, on click or on hover.

s.x: SpeedDial is a primary Fab that, when pressed, reveals several secondary actions as small labeled FABs, just like MUI’s SpeedDial. Use it when a screen’s primary action has three to six related variants (create document, spreadsheet, presentation). If there is only one action, use a Fab; if there are many options or they are not creation actions, use a Menu.

ariaLabel names the primary FAB and each SpeedDialAction takes an icon and a tooltipTitle. The component renders the FAB, the actions container and the labels. Accessible name for each action tooltipTitle creates the visible label and, if the action has no aria-label, is also used as its aria-label, so icon-only actions always have an accessible name. If tooltipTitle is not a string, pass aria-label yourself. When closed, the actions are invisible but still take up their space in the layout flow, as in MUI: place the SpeedDial in a corner with absolute or fixed positioning, for example with the utilities className="mtx-position-absolute mtx-right-0 mtx-bottom-0 mtx-m-2" inside a positioned container (see “Hidden and position”).
direction sets where the actions open: up (default), down, left or right. Vertically, labels appear to the left of each action; horizontally, above it. The arrow keys follow the direction.
color on the SpeedDial colors the primary FAB ( primary by default); on each SpeedDialAction, it colors that action ( secondary by default). Both accept the Fab colors.
Closed and open (the primary icon rotates 45°), hover, focus and disabled actions ( disabled). Escape closes it and returns focus to the FAB.

By default the labels of all actions are visible while the SpeedDial is open (MUI’s tooltipOpen), styled with the Tooltip tokens. With tooltipHover on the SpeedDial each action uses a real Tooltip that appears on hover or keyboard focus, to the left for vertical directions and above for horizontal ones; recommended for horizontal directions so labels do not overlap. On an action, tooltipOpen forces one mode and tooltipPlacement moves its Tooltip. Keyboard In both modes the label is visible while moving through the actions: in the persistent mode it always is, and with tooltipHover the Tooltip appears on keyboard focus and hides with Escape. Each action’s accessible name is still its aria-label (persistent labels are aria-hidden so they are not read twice).
event="hover" opens the SpeedDial when the mouse enters and closes it when it leaves. Clicking the FAB still toggles it, so it also works on touch screens and with the keyboard.

Without icon the FAB shows <SpeedDialIcon /> ( add), which rotates 45° when open. openIcon (on the SpeedDial or on SpeedDialIcon) replaces it with another icon while open: the closed icon rotates and fades out while the open one rotates into place. Icons can be Material Icons names or nodes such as an <svg> (24px).
Photo gallery: the SpeedDial is controlled, so each action performs its task and closes it.

hidden shrinks the primary FAB with a scale transition and closes the actions (for example while scrolling). position="fixed-br" and "fixed-bl" pin it 24px from the bottom-right or bottom-left corner of the viewport, above the content ( z-index 1050).
Grid panels (one per row on mobile, two from 900px), each with its SpeedDial in the corner.
The vanilla open(), close(), toggle() and direction become the open and direction props. In uncontrolled mode use defaultOpen; onOpen and onClose receive the event and the reason.
The CSS also works with plain markup (static HTML or server templates). Without the component you manage the state, aria-expanded, inert and the keyboard yourself.

d: Shows progress through a sequence of numbered steps, horizontal or vertical, linear or with clickable steps, plus its compact mobile version.

s.x: Stepper conveys progress through a process split into steps (sign-up, checkout, setup wizard): which step is active, which are completed and which are still ahead. Use it when order matters and each step makes sense on its own. Don’t use it to switch between views at the same level (use Tabs) or to show the progress of an ongoing operation (use Progress).

The shortest form is a <Stepper> with a steps array of labels. The component renders the semantic <ol>, the 24px numbered icon, the connectors and the accessible text (“Step 2 of 3”), and marks the active step with aria-current="step". defaultActiveStep (uncontrolled) or activeStep (controlled) is the zero-based index of the active step. Each entry of steps can also be an object with the Step props ( { label, optional, error, completed, disabled, icon, expanded, content }), or you can write <Step> children.

In linear mode (the default), steps before the active one are considered completed and the following ones disabled. useStepper() links a stepper through apiRef and exposes its state; StepperButton action="back|next|reset" drives it and disables itself on the first step ( back) or once finished ( next) unless keepEnabled; StepPanel shows the panel of the active step, and index="finished" the final panel once activeStep reaches the number of steps.
alternativeLabel places the label below the icon and splits the width evenly. It is the most robust option on narrow screens (horizontal only).

With nonLinear every step is a <button> (StepButton) with ripple, visible focus and activation with Enter or Space, and users can jump to any step. Completion is no longer inferred from the order: set it with completed or setCompleted().

orientation="vertical" stacks the steps. The children of a <Step label> become its StepContent, which expands with a transition only on the active step (or always, with expanded). Inside the stepper, a StepperButton without stepper acts on its own stepper.

By default the StepIcon is the step number. icon uses a custom Material Icon by name (24px, no forced size) or any node. A completed step shows a check and a step with an error shows a warning, replacing the icon.

Active, completed, optional ( optional, or a custom text), error with message ( error="message", or error without message) and disabled ( disabled). The connector before an active or completed step takes the primary color. Responsive behavior Below 600px, a horizontal stepper without alternative label only shows the label of the active step; the others are visually hidden but still available to screen readers. If every label must be visible on mobile, use alternativeLabel or the vertical orientation.

MobileStepper is MUI’s compact version: it renders the Back/Next buttons and a dots (default), text (“2 / 5”) or progress indicator (reusing LinearProgress). position="bottom|top" pins it to the edge of the window. backButton / nextButton replace the generated buttons with your own nodes; if they carry the mtx-mobile-stepper__back / mtx-mobile-stepper__next class, clicking them navigates.

An account sign-up wizard with validation: the cancelable onChange returns false to prevent moving forward while the TextField email is invalid, and marks the step and the field with an error ( setError(), error + helperText).
Inside Grid the stepper takes the width of its column; in narrow columns the alternative label or the vertical orientation work best.

apiRef exposes next(), back(), goTo(i), reset(), setCompleted(i, bool), setError(i, message|false), setDisabled(i, bool), isCompleted(i) and the activeStep, length and finished getters. Every change goes through onChange, which can cancel it.
The equivalent of the vanilla manual BEM usage: compose each Step with StepLabel (label, optional, icon) and StepContent. The connector is still generated.

A semantic <ol> is used: the order of the steps is part of the meaning. Name it with label or aria-label. The active step carries aria-current="step" (on the <li>, or on its <button> in non-linear mode). Each step includes hidden text with its position and state: “Step 2 of 3: Shipping, completed”. Icons and connectors are decorative ( aria-hidden). Texts are translated with the I18nProvider locale or the locale prop. In non-linear mode steps are native <button> elements with visible focus; disabled ones use disabled. In vertical, the content of collapsed steps is marked inert and aria-hidden so it cannot receive focus. MobileStepper announces the current step in an aria-live="polite" region; dots and the bar are decorative. Honors prefers-reduced-motion. Key Action Tab / Shift + Tab Moves through clickable steps (non-linear) and the Back/Next buttons. Enter / Space Activates the focused step or button.
